strategies.content: Implement a Master Framework Agreement to centralize definitions, interpretation principles, and common terms, incorporating them by reference into all other transaction documents to ensure consistency and reduce drafting redundancy.

Structure the funding model to utilize a multi-tranche capital structure (e.g., senior, mezzanine, and subordinated facilities) to finance the acquisition of receivables, optimizing the cost of capital and risk distribution.

Include a segregation of capacities clause ensuring that if a single entity acts in multiple roles (e.g., Servicer and Lender), its obligations and rights in each capacity are treated distinctively, except for self-noticing requirements.

Define strict eligibility criteria for Account Banks based on minimum credit ratings and regulatory authorization, and establish automatic replacement triggers upon rating downgrades or insolvency events to safeguard transaction funds.
Incorporate mechanisms for ad hoc subordinated funding to cover specific, pre-approved costs without triggering default, ensuring the issuer has liquidity for operational expenses.
Mandate regular Agreed Upon Procedures (AUP) audits of the Servicer and the underlying assets to independently verify the accuracy of reporting and compliance with eligibility criteria.

Clearly define Available Distribution Amounts to distinguish between funds available for revolving asset purchases versus funds available for periodic debt service and expense payments, preventing commingling of principal reinvestment and interest payment flows.
Appoint a Back-up Servicer at closing and define clear Invocation Plans to ensure seamless transfer of servicing operations upon a Servicer termination event, mitigating operational risk.

Explicitly list Basic Term Modifications (e.g., changes to maturity, principal, interest, priority of payments) that require unanimous or super-majority consent, protecting minority lenders from fundamental adverse changes.

Require the delivery of a Borrowing Base Report prior to any funding request to confirm that the value of eligible assets supports the requested advance after applying concentration limits and haircuts.

Establish a Cash Reserve Account funded to a target level (e.g., a percentage of the outstanding senior debt) to provide liquidity support for interest and senior expenses during periods of cash flow disruption.

Impose detailed Concentration Limits on the asset portfolio (e.g., limits on specific borrower types, modified loans, or payment methods) to prevent excessive exposure to higher-risk segments and ensure portfolio diversification.

Enforce a Coverage Requirement ensuring that interest rate hedging notionals track the outstanding principal balance of the rated notes (within a specific tolerance band) to mitigate interest rate mismatch risk.
Define standardized formulas for Delinquency and Default Rates based on rolling averages to smooth out volatility and serve as objective triggers for early amortization or cash trapping.

Include specific ESG Issue definitions covering environmental, labor, and corruption violations to trigger representations or repurchase obligations, aligning the transaction with responsible investment mandates.
Mandate a minimum Issuer Profit Amount to be retained annually by the special purpose vehicle to demonstrate commercial substance and tax residency in its jurisdiction of incorporation.

Implement dynamic Advance Rates that automatically reduce (increasing the haircut) if specific portfolio performance triggers (e.g., high delinquency or payment method changes) are breached, thereby increasing credit enhancement for senior tranches during stress.

Calculate the Net Eligible Receivables Balance by deducting Excess Concentration Amounts (assets exceeding portfolio limits) from the total eligible pool, ensuring that only diversified, compliant assets support the debt issuance.

Implement a 'Most Senior Lender' control mechanism where voting rights and instructions to the Security Trustee shift dynamically based on which class of debt is currently the most senior outstanding, ensuring that the primary risk-holders control enforcement decisions.

Establish dynamic concentration limits for specific borrower risk profiles (e.g., near-prime or subprime) and apply 'Advance Rate Reduction' mechanisms (haircuts) if these limits are exceeded or if portfolio performance metrics deteriorate.

Utilize separate ledgers within Pre-Funding Accounts for different tranches of debt (e.g., Senior and Mezzanine) to ensure clear tracking and application of unused proceeds for each specific class of notes.

Define 'Principal Amount Outstanding' to explicitly account for initial subscriptions, subsequent advances, and rescinded payments, ensuring accurate liability tracking particularly when principal payments must be returned or are rescinded.

Structure redemption amounts to vary based on the transaction phase, utilizing a borrowing base cap during the revolving period and a full priority-of-payments waterfall during the amortization or post-enforcement periods.
Define 'Qualifying Lenders' based on tax residence or treaty status to prevent the Issuer from incurring withholding tax liabilities, and restrict transfers only to entities meeting these criteria.

Include specific triggers for 'Recharacterization Events' in transactions involving jurisdictions with distinct legal systems (e.g., Scotland or Northern Ireland) to address risks where local law might override the governing law of the contract.
Establish a 'Permitted Modification' regime that allows for minor, technical, or regulatory amendments without requiring full lender consent, while retaining veto rights for material changes.

Freeze underwriting and servicing standards at closing by defining 'Seller Documentation and Policies' via reference to a static data room index, preventing unauthorized drift in credit quality or servicing procedures.
Implement a 'Pro Rata Share' calculation that bases allocation on Commitments during the availability period and on Principal Amounts Outstanding after the availability period or upon default.

Mandate the delivery of a 'List of Receivables' and satisfaction of specific conditions (such as solvency and no default) as a prerequisite for any 'Purchase Date' to ensure the validity of the asset transfer.
Calculate the 'Borrowing Base' by deducting 'Excess Concentration Amounts' (receivables exceeding specific portfolio limits) from the eligible pool before applying the advance rate.

Use a 'Subordinated Facility' not only for credit enhancement but also as a liquidity mechanism to fund the purchase price of receivables, utilizing 'Subordinated Settlement Dates' to net off obligations.

Define 'Repurchase Price' to include not just the outstanding principal balance but also accrued interest, fees, and breakage costs to ensure the Issuer is made whole when ineligible assets are removed.

Implement a master framework agreement to incorporate common definitions, interpretation rules, and boilerplate provisions (such as calculations, payments, and jurisdiction) by reference into all other transaction documents to ensure consistency and reduce drafting redundancy.
Define distinct priority of payment waterfalls for pre-enforcement and post-enforcement scenarios to dictate how funds are distributed under normal operations versus distressed conditions.

Establish a mechanism for extending the scheduled termination date that allows individual lenders to accept or reject the extension, with specific provisions for exiting or buying out rejecting lenders while the facility continues for accepting lenders.

Include 'Basic Term Modification' clauses that require unanimous consent from all funded classes for material changes (rates, dates, amounts), while allowing less material amendments to proceed with lower consent thresholds.
Implement disenfranchisement clauses that prevent lenders affiliated with the originator or borrower from voting on enforcement, waivers, or significant instructions to avoid conflicts of interest.
Include standstill provisions requiring junior creditors to refrain from taking independent enforcement action for a specified period to allow senior creditors to control the enforcement strategy.
Grant junior creditors a purchase option (call option) to buy out senior debt at par following an enforcement event, allowing them to take control of the collateral and protect their residual value.

Incorporate exclusivity or right-of-first-refusal provisions requiring the originator to offer a minimum percentage of eligible receivables or future financing opportunities to the current investors before approaching third parties.

Establish a formal process for amending eligibility criteria and concentration limits that requires written consent and updated schedules, allowing the transaction to adapt to changing portfolio characteristics.

Include loss-sharing and turnover provisions to ensure that if any lender receives a payment in excess of its pro-rata share (e.g., through set-off or separate recovery), it holds the excess in trust and redistributes it to the other lenders.
Mandate the maintenance of hedging arrangements (such as interest rate swaps) to mitigate market risks, including requirements for the replacement of swap providers upon rating downgrades or default.

Include strict representations and undertakings regarding risk retention to ensure the originator retains a material net economic interest in the securitization as required by applicable regulations (e.g., EU/UK Securitisation Regulations, US Risk Retention Rules).

Require the originator and issuer to comply with regulatory transparency and reporting requirements, including the provision of data tapes and transaction summaries to competent authorities and investors.
Utilize payment set-off mechanisms between the purchase price of receivables and proceeds from subordinated loans to minimize physical cash movements and operational friction on closing dates.

Provide comprehensive indemnities to agents, trustees, and lenders covering losses, break costs, currency conversion risks, and tax liabilities, while excluding losses resulting from gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.
Include 'increased costs' indemnities to compensate lenders for reductions in return or increased capital requirements resulting from changes in law or regulation (e.g., Basel III/IV implementation).

Include tax gross-up provisions requiring the payer to increase payments if withholding taxes are imposed, ensuring the payee receives the full amount due, alongside tax credit reimbursement mechanisms to prevent unjust enrichment.

Establish a strict order of application for partial payments received, typically prioritizing fee and expense reimbursement before interest and principal, to ensure administrative parties are paid first.
Establish clear protocols for updating contact details for notices, ensuring changes are effective only after a specified notice period to prevent communication gaps.
Mandate the use of a common language (e.g., English) for all transaction documents and notices, requiring certified translations for any exceptions to ensure clarity and enforceability.
Include robust non-waiver provisions ensuring that delays in exercising rights do not constitute a waiver of those rights, and require all waivers to be in writing to be effective.
Implement a formal amendment process requiring written consent from relevant parties, with specific mechanics for 'Basic Term Modifications' or changes affecting payment priorities.

Incorporate pre-agreed amendment mechanics for benchmark rate replacement (e.g., transitioning from IBOR to risk-free rates) to allow for efficient updates to interest calculations without full unanimity.
Utilize 'entire agreement' clauses to supersede prior engagement letters or understandings, limiting reliance to representations expressly set out in the final transaction documents.
Explicitly exclude personal liability of officers, directors, and agents of the issuer, clarifying that obligations are solely corporate to protect individuals from recourse.
Incorporate non-petition covenants prohibiting transaction parties from initiating insolvency proceedings against the special purpose vehicle (Issuer) to preserve bankruptcy remoteness.
Embed limited recourse provisions restricting claims against the Issuer solely to available funds in the priority of payments, extinguishing any shortfall after asset realization.
Restrict assignment of rights and obligations to ensure stability of counterparties, while allowing specific exceptions for security trustees, facility agents, or securitization-specific transfers.

Define comprehensive confidentiality obligations with specific carve-outs for regulatory disclosure (e.g., Securitisation Regulation, Rule 17g-5) and rating agencies to facilitate compliance and market functioning.
Include acknowledgments regarding Special Resolution Regimes (e.g., FDIC powers) to ensure enforceability of Qualified Financial Contracts and cross-border recognition of resolution stays.
Insert contractual recognition of bail-in powers by resolution authorities to comply with banking regulations and ensure liabilities can be written down or converted during bank resolution.
Designate exclusive jurisdiction for disputes to ensure legal certainty, while retaining the right for finance parties to enforce judgments in other jurisdictions if necessary.

Structure a comprehensive Conditions Precedent checklist requiring constitutional documents, solvency certificates, corporate resolutions, and legal opinions (capacity, enforceability, true sale, tax) before funding.
Define granular eligibility criteria for receivables, including requirements for origination in the ordinary course, no default/delinquency, and full disbursement.
Prioritize automated payment methods (e.g., salary deduction, direct debit) in eligibility criteria to minimize collection risk, with strict limits on less secure payment methods.
Require representations that assets are free from set-off, counterclaims, or litigation to ensure the Issuer has clear title and enforceable rights.
Establish concentration limits to diversify portfolio risk, capping exposure to specific obligors, payment methods, or credit grades (e.g., subprime vs. prime).
Include mechanisms for temporary waivers of concentration limit breaches, subject to specific conditions and timeframes, to allow flexibility during portfolio ramp-up or stress.
Set performance triggers based on delinquency rates, default rates, and excess spread levels to detect asset deterioration early and trigger corrective actions or early amortization.
Define specific events of default for the Seller/Servicer, including non-payment, breach of obligations, and regulatory sanctions, to trigger replacement or enforcement.
Impose financial covenants on the Seller (e.g., Tangible Net Worth, Liquidity) to ensure ongoing solvency and alignment of interest throughout the transaction life.

Design detailed pre-enforcement and post-enforcement priority of payments (waterfalls) to structure cash flows, ensuring senior expenses and interest are paid before junior tranches and equity returns.
Prioritize tax, trustee fees, and servicing fees at the top of the payment waterfall to ensure operational continuity and regulatory compliance before debt service.
Require the appointment of a back-up servicer and define triggers for their invocation to ensure business continuity if the primary servicer fails.

Require representations verifying that no transaction proceeds will be used to fund sanctioned entities or activities, and that parties have implemented and maintained compliance policies regarding sanctions and anti-money laundering for a specified look-back period.

Include comprehensive data protection representations confirming compliance with privacy laws, specifically regarding cross-border data transfers, appropriate safeguards, and the absence of historical breaches or regulatory investigations.

Mandate that the Issuer and Seller maintain their Centre of Main Interests (COMI) in a specific jurisdiction and do not have establishments elsewhere to ensure predictable insolvency treatment and tax residence stability.

Obligate the Seller to segregate sold receivables in their books, records, and IT systems, clearly identifying them as sold to the Issuer to prevent commingling risks and facilitate separation in insolvency.
Include a 'No Adverse Selection' warranty ensuring the Seller does not select inferior assets for the securitization portfolio compared to the eligible receivables remaining on their own books.

Establish 'Further Assurance' undertakings requiring the Seller to execute additional documents necessary to perfect the Issuer's title or security interest, particularly upon the occurrence of specific regulatory recharacterization events in relevant jurisdictions.
Enforce strict negative covenants on the Issuer (SPV) prohibiting employees, subsidiaries, unrelated business activities, dividend distributions, and VAT grouping to maintain bankruptcy remoteness.

Structure the Security Trustee's duties to act primarily on the direction of an 'Instructing Creditor,' limiting the Trustee's independent discretion and protecting them from liability when following such instructions.
Prohibit individual creditors from taking direct enforcement action against the Issuer, vesting the sole right to enforce security and transaction documents in the Security Trustee.

Empower the Security Trustee to suspend action, including enforcement or litigation, until sufficient indemnification, security, or pre-funding is provided by creditors to cover potential liabilities and costs.

Require the Security Trustee to obtain independent financial advice regarding the sufficiency of potential recoveries before disposing of secured assets post-enforcement, unless instructed otherwise by creditors after a failure to obtain such advice.

Supplement statutory trustee powers to explicitly allow the Security Trustee to rely on expert advice, certificates from directors, and unverified electronic instructions without incurring liability for errors or lack of authenticity.
Ensure collection accounts are free of encumbrances and set-off rights, with strict provisions that funds are only withdrawn in accordance with the transaction documents.
Include specific representations that the transaction documents are entered into on arm's length commercial terms and in good faith to protect against clawback risks in insolvency scenarios.

Limit the liability of administrative parties (such as Security Trustees) by expressly excluding any obligation to monitor or supervise third-party service providers, allowing them to assume due performance absent written notice of breach.

Empower trustees and agents to seek instructions from controlling creditors or obtain expert advice at the issuer's expense to mitigate decision-making risk, without liability for delays caused by seeking such input.
Protect administrative parties from tax liability by authorizing required tax withholdings from payments without imposing an obligation on them to gross up those payments.

Absolve trustees and agents of responsibility for verifying the accuracy, sufficiency, or validity of legal opinions, due diligence reports, or third-party data provided in connection with the transaction.

Grant trustees the discretion to evaluate the sufficiency of offered indemnities or pre-funding based on worst-case scenarios, including potential litigation costs in multiple jurisdictions, before taking requested actions.
Limit trustee and agent liability to instances of gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud, expressly excluding ordinary negligence to encourage willingness to act.

Include robust non-reliance clauses requiring secured creditors to confirm they have conducted independent risk appraisals and investigations rather than relying on the trustee or agents for due diligence.
Authorize trustees and agents to delegate functions to reputable third parties, limiting liability for the delegate's default provided due care was exercised in their selection.

Include safeguards preventing trustees from being forced to perform regulated activities (e.g., under financial services laws) unless properly authorized, allowing delegation of such functions if necessary.

Waive potential conflicts of interest to allow trustees and agents to engage in separate commercial banking, advisory, or trading relationships with transaction parties without accounting for profits.

Exclude liability for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages (including loss of profit) for administrative parties, regardless of notice or foreseeability, and limit liability to actual direct loss.

Establish a mechanism for trustee or agent resignation that allows the retiring party to appoint a successor if the issuer fails to do so within a specified timeframe, ensuring continuity of administration.
Centralize enforcement rights in the security trustee to prevent chaotic, individual creditor actions, prohibiting individual creditors from enforcing security independently.
Implement turnover provisions requiring any creditor who receives payments outside the agreed priority of payments to hold such funds in trust and immediately transfer them to the security trustee.
Explicitly define the facility agent's role as solely mechanical and administrative to avoid the implication of fiduciary duties or discretionary decision-making authority.

Establish a clear hierarchy of instructions (e.g., acting on Most Senior Lender direction) and absolve the agent of liability for acting or refraining from acting in accordance with such binding instructions.
Include erroneous payment clawback provisions requiring recipients to return funds paid by the agent in error on demand, with interest and free of set-off or defenses.
Structure a back-stop indemnity where lenders or noteholders agree to indemnify the agent or trustee pro-rata if the issuer fails to satisfy its indemnification obligations.
Utilize standardized deeds of accession to allow new parties (e.g., new lenders, swap providers) to join existing framework agreements seamlessly without re-executing the main documents.

definitions.content: “ABS Transaction” means any securitisation of any Receivables originated by the Seller, which involves the marketing and distribution of securities in the public markets.

ABS Transaction Fee: means a fee payable to the Senior Lenders or other financing parties in the event of a voluntary cancellation or prepayment of the facility for the purposes of entering into a public ABS Transaction (securitization take-out).

“Acceding Swap Provider Minimum Rating” means, in relation to a new or successor Swap Provider that is not an affiliate of Swap Provider, a rating for its long-term unsecured and non-credit-enhanced debt obligations of A or higher by S&P or Fitch or A2 or higher by Moody’s.

Acceptance: means the formal acceptance by the Purchaser (Issuer) of an Offer to sell Receivables from the Seller, typically triggering the sale and transfer of such Receivables under the Receivables Purchase Agreement.

“Accession Date” means, in respect of any party, the date on which it accedes to: if it is an acceding Senior Lender, the Senior Facility Agreement and the Master Framework Agreement, in accordance with clause 18 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Senior Facility Agreement; if it is an acceding Mezzanine Note Purchaser or another member of a Mezzanine Note Purchaser Group, the Mezzanine Facility Agreement and the Master Framework Agreement, in accordance with clause 12 (Increase of the Mezzanine Commitments) or clause 13 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement; or if is an acceding Swap Provider, in accordance with Clause 3.47 (Accession of a new or successor Swap Provider) of the Master Framework Agreement.

Account Acceleration Notice: means a notice delivered by the Cash Manager or Security Trustee to an Account Bank instructing it to block or transfer funds, typically following a default or enforcement event.
“Account Bank” means any Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as the context requires.
“Account Bank Downgrade” means, in respect of any Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, the point in time when it ceases to be an Account Bank Eligible Institution.

“Account Bank Eligible Institution” means any Issuer Account Bank, Collections Account Bank or any proposed Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as at any date of determination, that: is and remains duly authorised in respect of its deposit taking activities under the laws of the jurisdiction in which it is operating; and if it is not an Electronic Money Institution, maintains certain corporate ratings, which are short term unsecured, unguaranteed and unsubordinated debt obligations rated at least P-1 by Moody’s, A-l by S&P and F-1 by Fitch; or if it is an Electronic Money Institution, is an Approved Electronic Money Institution.

“Account Bank Event” means, in respect of an Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, any of: the occurrence of an Insolvency Event; it being or becoming subject to Insolvency Proceedings; to the extent such Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank is an Electronic Money Institution, an “insolvency event” occurs with respect to it or it becomes subject to “insolvency proceedings”, each as defined in the Electronic Money Regulations 2011/99; to the extent that such Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank is an Electronic Money Institution as at the date on which it is appointed to act as an Account Bank for the purposes of this Transaction, on any subsequent date it is no longer registered or authorised as an Electronic Money Institution; the occurrence of an Account Bank Downgrade; or any event of default (or equivalent event) or breach by the Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as the case may be, is continuing in respect of the relevant account bank under the Issuer Account Bank Agreement or any Acknowledgment of Collections Account Declaration of Trust executed by the account bank.
“Account Mandate” means any account mandate (including any account terms and conditions) in relation to the Issuer Accounts or the Collections Account.

“Acknowledgment of Collections Account Declaration of Trust” means an acknowledgment of the creation of a trust over a Collections Account substantially in the form set out in a Collections Account Declaration of Trust.

“Adjusted Loan Terms” means, in respect of any Receivable and its related Consumer Loan, that it has been originated in circumstances in which the Borrower had originally specified an amount of borrowing and term of the loan at the time the Borrower applied for the Consumer Loan and the Seller subsequently offered to that Borrower an option to adjust the loan terms by increasing or decreasing the amount of borrowing and/or the term of the proposed Consumer Loan and the Borrower consequently adjusted the terms of their initial application.

Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage: means the maximum permitted percentage of the Portfolio, as specified in the Concentration Limits, that may consist of Receivables from Prime Borrowers with Adjusted Loan Terms.

Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the portion of the aggregate Principal Balance of Receivables from Prime Borrowers with Adjusted Loan Terms that exceeds the Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage.
“Affected Person” means the Facility Agent, the Security Trustee, any Senior Lender, any Mezzanine Note Purchaser, any Mezzanine Funding Agent and any Swap Provider.

Agreed Ad Hoc Funding Amount: means, as at any Cut-Off Date, any Subordinated Advances made by the Subordinated Lender to fund specified ad hoc costs payable by the Issuer in accordance with the Transaction Documents which are pre-approved in writing by the Facility Agent (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, including where withholding consent would prevent the remediation of an Early Amortisation Event) or any other costs and expenses related to transaction purposes as specified in the Subordinated Facility Agreement.

“Agreed Adjusted Ad Hoc Funding Amount” means, as at any Cut-Off Date, an amount equal to the higher of: zero; and an amount equal to: the aggregate Agreed Ad Hoc Funding Amounts incurred from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date; and the aggregate of the amounts calculated under paragraph (ii)(A)(2)(cc) of the definition of Subordinated Redemption Amount, from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date.

“Appointee” means any attorney, manager, agent, delegate, receiver or other person appointed by the Security Trustee under the Security Trustee Provisions or the Transaction Security or by the Facility Agent under the Transaction Documents, including to discharge any of the Security Trustee’s or Facility Agent’s functions or advise in relation thereto.

Approved Electronic Money Institution: means each Electronic Money Institution that has been approved in writing by the Facility Agent (acting on the instructions of all Funders) (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed) to be an Account Bank from time to time.

Assignment Agreement: means an agreement typically in the form set out in a schedule to the Facility Agreement, pursuant to which a Lender or Noteholder assigns or transfers its rights and obligations to a new party.

“AUP Audit” means an audit of the Servicer and the Receivables on agreed upon procedures designated by the Facility Agent (acting on the instructions of each of the Senior Lenders and the Mezzanine Funding Agent) acting reasonably.
“AUP Report” means the written reports delivered by the accountants recording the results of any AUP Audit.
“Automatic Subordinated Advance” means an automatic further advance under the Subordinated Facility in accordance with the Subordinated Facility Agreement;

“Available Distribution Amount” means, as at the applicable Cut-Off Date that relates to a Borrowing Base Report, an amount equal to: for the purposes of determining funds that may be applied towards Initial Purchase Price on any Purchase Date other than a Monthly Payment Date or the payment of Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount on any Weekly Utilisation Date, the amount (without double counting) equal to the sum of the amount standing to the credit of: prior to the Issuer Collections Account Effective Date, the Transaction Account and the Pre-Funding Account; and from (and including) the Issuer Collections Account Effective Date: the Issuer Collections Account and the Pre-Funding Account; and any amounts requested by the Issuer under a Senior Utilisation Request or Mezzanine Funding Request pursuant to the terms of any Facility Agreement which will be credited to the Transaction Account: provided, in each case, that it shall not include any amounts advanced to the Issuer for the purposes of crediting the Pre-Funding Account or Cash Reserve Account; and in respect of the payment of the Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount on a Weekly Utilisation Date, on the relevant Weekly Utilisation Date; in respect of the payment of Initial Purchase Price on a Purchase Date, on the relevant Purchase Date, for the purposes of calculating the available funds to be applied on any Monthly Payment Date in accordance with the applicable Priority of Payments, the amount (without double counting) equal to the sum of: the sum of all amounts standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (other than amounts standing to the credit of the Issuer Profit Ledger), Issuer Collections Account and the Cash Reserve Account including, following the occurrence of a Security Enforcement Event, any other proceeds from the enforcement of security over the Purchased Receivables; any amounts requested by the Issuer under a Senior Utilisation Request, Mezzanine Funding Request pursuant to the terms of any Facility Agreement which will stand to the credit of the Transaction Account for the purpose of financing the acquisition of Receivables on any Monthly Payment Date in accordance with the Priority of Payments, provided that it shall not include any amounts advanced to the Issuer for the purposes of crediting the Pre-Funding Account or Cash Reserve Account; on any Monthly Payment Date, any amount to be received by the Issuer from a Swap Provider in accordance with any Swap Agreement, other than amounts described in paragraph (iv) below; any amount to be received by the Issuer from a Swap Provider in accordance with any Swap Agreement which is a Swap Termination Amount which is not required to be applied to purchase a replacement swap transaction and any amount described in clause 15.2 (Premium Received by the Issuer) or clause 15.3 (Termination payment received by the Issuer) of the Cash Management Agreement; plus in respect of any Monthly Payment Date occurring during the period from the Closing Date to the date that is six months after the Closing Date, amounts advanced under the Subordinated Facility to be applied pursuant to any of items 1 to 19 of the Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments, and at any other time, amounts requested by the Issuer (or the Servicer acting on its behalf) under a Subordinated Utilisation Request pursuant to the terms of the Subordinated Facility Agreement which will stand to the credit of the Transaction Account.

Back-up Servicer: means the entity appointed to act as the back-up servicer under the Back-up Servicing Agreement, being the party responsible for assuming the servicing of the Receivables upon the termination of the Servicer's appointment.

Back-up Servicer Invocation Notice: means the notice delivered to the Back-up Servicer (often termed a 'Standby Servicer Invocation Notice' in the Back-up Servicing Agreement) instructing it to assume the role of successor Servicer.

“Basic Term Modification” means: any amendment to the Programme Scheduled Termination Date or the Commitments other than: any explicit right to cancel, reduce, extend or increase the Commitments already included within the terms of the Transaction Documents; or any explicit right to extend or renew the Programme Scheduled Termination Date included within the Transaction Documents; any amendment made to the date of maturity or the date of payment of any Senior Facility, any Mezzanine Note or any Subordinated Facility; any amendment to the currency of any payment under any Transaction Document; any amendment to or waiver of a Potential Early Amortisation Event, an Early Amortisation Event, a Potential Servicer Termination Event or a Servicer Termination Event (other than any waiver relating to a breach of the Senior Borrowing Base or the Senior Advance Rate Reduction Event Borrowing Base, which shall be a decision solely for the Senior Lenders, and any waiver relating to a breach of the Mezzanine Borrowing Base, which shall be a decision solely for the Mezzanine Note Purchasers); any amendment to the definition of Senior Repayment Amount that would result in the repayment of any Senior Loan (in whole or in part) on a date earlier than its expected date of repayment; any amendment to the definition of Mezzanine Redemption Amount that would result in the repayment of any Mezzanine Note (in whole or in part) on a date earlier than its expected date of maturity or payment (as the case may be); any amendment to the definitions of Most Senior Lender Instruction and Most Senior Lenders; any amendment to or waiver of any Event of Default or Mezzanine Event of Default provided that any waiver of an Event of Default will be solely at the discretion of the Senior Lenders and any waiver of a Mezzanine Event of Default will be solely at the discretion of the Mezzanine Note Purchasers; any amendment to or waiver of any Concentration Limit on any date of determination; any amendment to or waiver of any of the Eligibility Criteria on any date of determination; any amendment to delete, remove or modify any representation, warranty or undertaking given by the Issuer, the Seller, the Servicer or the Subordinated Lender in a manner which is prejudicial to any Senior Lender or any Mezzanine Note Purchaser; any amendment to the principal and/or interest on the Senior Facility; any amendment to the definition of “Mezzanine Advance Rate”; any amendment to any Priority of Payments; any amendment to the principal and/or interest on the Mezzanine Notes; any amendment to the terms providing for the resignation, replacement and appointment of any Transaction Party; any amendment to the definition of “Change of Control” or any waiver of any Change of Control; any amendment to the terms of enforcement of any Transaction Security; any release of any of the Secured Property (other than as explicitly contemplated in the Transaction Documents); any amendment to Clause 3.41 (Recovering Funding Party and Sharing Payment) of the Master Framework Agreement; or any amendment to this definition.

“Borrower Agreement” means any agreement between the Seller and a Borrower which records the entire agreement and terms between the parties with respect to the Consumer Loan advanced by the Seller to the Borrower, from time to time, in accordance with the terms of that agreement.

Borrowing Base Report: means a report delivered by the Servicer setting out the calculation of the Borrowing Base, the details of the Receivables, and compliance with Eligibility Criteria and Concentration Limits as at a Cut-Off Date.
“Cash Reserve” means the cash reserve to be maintained in, and standing to the credit of, the Cash Reserve Account.

Cash Reserve Account: means the reserve account in the name of the Issuer designated in writing by each relevant Seller, Issuer and the Facility Agent, from time to time, to fall within this definition and maintained at all times at an Account Bank Eligible Institution.

“Cash Reserve Target Amount” means, as at any date of determination, an amount equal to: as at any date occurring prior to the end of the Revolving Period, 0.75 per cent of the aggregate Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date (after taking account of any increase or decrease of the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding that day); and as at any date occurring after the end of the Revolving Period, zero.
“Class” means any class of loans or notes, with each of the Senior Loans, the Mezzanine Notes and the Subordinated Loan being a separate class.

“Collections” means, in respect of any Purchased Receivable: all cash collections and other cash proceeds of the Receivable in respect of the relevant Borrower Agreement, including, without limitation, all finance charges (if any), all VAT (if any) and cash proceeds of any Related Rights; any proceeds received by the Seller of the Receivable from insurance policies; any Deemed Collection relating to the Purchased Receivable; any proceeds from the sale of the Purchased Receivable received by the Issuer from any third party; any amounts paid to a Collections Account in respect of any Purchased Receivable that becomes a Top-Up Receivable; any amounts paid to the Issuer by the Swap Provider; and any Repurchase Price paid to the Issuer by the Seller in respect of the Purchased Receivable in connection with any permitted repurchase of the Purchased Receivable.
“Commitment” means the Senior Commitment or the Mezzanine Commitment, as the context requires.

Conditions Precedent to Utilisation: means the documentary and factual conditions that must be satisfied or waived before a lender is obliged to advance funds under a facility, typically including valid borrowing requests, no default continuing, representations remaining true, and satisfaction of eligibility criteria for the assets being funded.
“Consumer Loan” means any unsecured personal loan offered or provided by the Seller to its customers in the ordinary course of its business.

“Coverage Requirement” means the requirement that: each of the Swap Agreements entered into by the Issuer (as applicable) is in full force and effect and has not been terminated; and the Swap Agreements entered into by the Issuer and the related Hedge Transactions have a notional that covers at least 90 per cent. and no more than 110 per cent. of the total Senior Principal Amount Outstanding on a Hedging Test Date.

Crystallisation Notice: means a notice delivered by the Security Trustee to the Issuer (or other charging company) effectively converting a floating charge over assets into a fixed charge, typically served upon the occurrence of an Event of Default or to protect the security assets from jeopardy.

“Cut-Off Date” means: in respect of any Borrowing Base Report, 11.59 pm on either the day prior, or two days prior, to the Borrowing Base Reporting Date, on which the relevant Borrowing Base Report is to be delivered; or in respect of any Monthly Servicer Report, all information available to the Servicer for the purposes of reporting at 11:59 pm on the day, or two days, immediately preceding the Monthly Servicer Report Date on which the Monthly Servicer Report is to be delivered.

Deemed Collections: means amounts that the Seller is deemed to have received and must pay to the Issuer, typically representing reductions in the outstanding balance of a receivable due to non-cash credits such as merchandise returns, disputed amounts, dilutive items, set-offs, or breaches of representations and warranties, rather than actual cash payments from the borrower.

“Default Rate” means, on any Determination Date, in respect of the Collection Period ending on that date, the rate (expressed as a percentage) equal to the quotient of: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that have become Defaulted Receivables during that Collection Period; and the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are not Defaulted Receivables, as of the end of the fourth Collection Period preceding that Collection Period.

“Defaulted Receivable” means, in respect of any Receivable, as follows: it remains unpaid past its due date for a period equal to, or more than, 90 days; that the Servicer has identified, in accordance with the relevant Seller Documentation and Policies, to be a Receivable which is uncollectable or that should be written off as such if it has not previously been written off; or that has otherwise been written off in accordance with the relevant Accounting Principles.

“Deferred Purchase Price” means, on any Monthly Payment Date in respect of Purchased Receivables, an amount equal to the Available Distribution Amount remaining to make the payment under the final paragraph of the relevant Priority of Payments.

“Delinquency Rate” means, on any Determination Date, in respect of the Collection Period ending on that date, the rate (expressed as a percentage) equal to the quotient of: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are Delinquent Receivables; and the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are not Defaulted Receivables, as of the end of the third Collection Period preceding that Collection Period.

“Delinquent Receivable” means, in respect of any Receivable, it remains unpaid past its due date for a period equal to, or more than, 31 days but less than 90 days, provided that: any Receivable that remains unpaid past its due date for a period equal to, or more than, 31 days solely as a consequence of a systems failure or other technical failure that prevents the affected Employer Partner from making the relevant payment and/or [PARTY_NAME] from reconciling the funds received by it from an Employer Partner (provided that, once the Employer Partner has resolved the systems failure or other technical failure or has otherwise sent the relevant information to [PARTY_NAME], [PARTY_NAME] has not failed to reconcile such funds within two Business Days of such resolution or receipt of information) shall, subject to paragraph (b) below, not constitute a Delinquent Receivable; and the systems failure or other technical failure referred to in sub-paragraph (a) above must be remedied within a period of 31 days of the Servicer becoming aware of such failure or being notified of the same by the Employer Partner.

Determination Date: means the last day of each calendar month or such other date specified in the transaction documents on which determinations regarding the portfolio (such as borrowing base or performance metrics) are made.

Early Amortisation Event: means the occurrence of specific events that trigger the end of the revolving period and the commencement of the early amortisation period, typically including performance triggers (such as high delinquency or default rates), servicer termination events, issuer insolvency, or failure to maintain required reserves.

Eligible Receivable: means, as at any date of determination, any Purchased Receivable satisfying the specified eligibility criteria, which typically include requirements regarding enforceability, compliance with laws, absence of defaults, and conformity with credit and underwriting policies.
“Employer Partner” means any employer that has entered into an Employer Service Agreement with [PARTY_NAME].

“Encumbrance” means: any Security Interest; arrangement under which money or claims to money, or the benefit of, a bank or other account may be applied, set off or made subject to a combination of accounts so as to effect discharge of any sum owed or payable to any person; or any other type of preferential arrangement (including any title transfer and retention arrangement) having a similar effect.
“Facilities” means the Senior Facility, the Mezzanine Facility and the Subordinated Facility, as the context requires.
“Final Maturity Date” means the first Monthly Payment Date falling 60 months after the end of the Revolving Period.
“Funding Request” means, as the context requires, any Senior Utilisation Request or any Mezzanine Funding Request.
“Further Advance” means any further advance under a Purchased Receivable pursuant to the relevant Borrower Agreement.

“Hedging Test Date” means the day falling on the date set out in paragraph (a) of the definition of Monthly Payment Date (or such other date as may be agreed between each of the Seller, the Original Senior Lender, the Mezzanine Funding Agent, the Swap Provider and the Issuer in writing (which may be by email) from time to time).
“Initial PurchasePrice” means, with respect to any Receivable, the Outstanding Principal Balance of the Receivable as of the Determination Date immediately preceding its Purchase Date.

“Issuer Account Bank Agreement” means the shifting control acknowledgement dated on or about the Signing Date between, among others, the Issuer Account Bank, the Issuer and the Cash Manager relating to the Transaction Account, the Pre-Funding Account, the Issuer Collections Account and the Cash Reserve Account or any other agreement designated as falling within this definition by the Servicer, the Issuer, the Facility Agent and the Security Trustee from time to time, by agreement in writing.

“Issuer Profit Amount” means GBP 1,200 per annum, credited in equal portions on each Monthly Payment Date to the Issuer Profit Ledger and to be retained (subject to the payment by the Issuer therefrom of any corporation tax due from the Issuer in respect of its profits) by the Issuer as profit in respect of the business of the Issuer.

“List of Receivables” means an excel spreadsheet issued in “read only” format recording the Receivables purchased or to be purchased by the Issuer from the Seller in accordance with clause 2.1 (Agreement to sell and purchase Receivables) of the Receivables Purchase Agreement and substantially in the form set out in Schedule 4 (Form of List of Receivables) to the Receivables Purchase Agreement with the fields agreed in writing between the Seller and the Facility Agent from time to time, which shall include, among other things, the Borrower Agreement ID, the loan start date of the relevant Borrower Agreement, the Outstanding Principal Balance of Receivables as at the relevant Origination Date and if the relevant Receivable is a Scottish Receivable that is, or will be, subject to a Scottish Trust.

“Majority Senior Lenders” means: while any member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document: on any date during the Revolving Period, each member of the Original Senior Lender Group that is party to any Transaction Document (notwithstanding the proportion of the Senior Total Commitments that their related Senior Commitments comprise); or from (and including) the Termination Date, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose aggregate Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of all Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date, provided that, if any member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document, the consent of that member of the Original Senior Lender Group that is party to any Transaction Document shall also be required; or if no member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document: on any date during the Revolving Period, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose Senior Commitments on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of the Senior Total Commitments on that date; or from (and including) the Termination Date, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose aggregate Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of all Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date.

“Mezzanine Advance Rate” means, as at any date of determination, the weighted average percentage that is calculated by applying the following, as relevant: 95 per cent. for the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Eligible Receivables, excluding any Receivables falling within the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; and 70.5 per cent. for the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount, in each case, as at that date.

“Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event” means, as at any Determination Date, any of the following events: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding in respect of Borrowers that are paying by way of direct debit or Push Payments for at least two consecutive calendar months ending on that Determination Date (rather than by way of Salary Deduction), excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been delinquent for more than 90 days, is greater than 19.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables, excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been outstanding for more than 90 days; the Default Rate across the most recent consecutive three-month period is greater than 1.25 per cent., as calculated on each relevant Determination Date; or the Default Rate across the most recent consecutive three-month period is greater than 0.75 per cent., as calculated on each relevant Determination Date, provided that, following the occurrence of (a) and/or (b) and/or (c), where the relevant breach, or breaches, has, or have, been remedied and no further breach has occurred for at least three consecutive Determination Dates, no reduction to the Mezzanine Advance Rate shall apply (and no waiver in this respect shall be required).

“Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event Borrowing Base” means, on any Monthly Payment Date, any Funding Request Date, any Funding Date and any Purchase Date, without double-counting or double-deduction, an amount equal to: the product of: the percentage that is equal to: the Mezzanine Advance Rate; less the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage; and the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance as at that date; plus the sum of: the balance standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Transaction Account on that date); the balance standing to the credit of the Issuer Collections Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Issuer Collections Account on that date); and the balance standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Pre-Funding Account on that date); less the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date.

“Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage” means: 5.0 per cent., which shall be applicable if a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraphs (a) or (b) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event; or 2.5 per cent, which shall be applicable if a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraph (c) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event and no Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraphs (a) or (b) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event.

“Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage Redemption Amount” means, on any Monthly Payment Date on which a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, subject to funds being available for that purpose following the application of the Available Distribution Amount to all items senior to the repayment of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage Repayment Amount in the relevant Priority of Payments, the amount by which the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date (after taking account of any redemptions that day), exceeds the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event Borrowing Base as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date.

“Mezzanine Available Commitments” means, at any time, the amount equal to: the Mezzanine Facilities Limit; less the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding under the Mezzanine Notes at that time.

“Mezzanine Borrowing Base” means: on any Monthly Payment Date, any Funding Request Date, any Funding Date and any Purchase Date when no Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, without double-counting or double-deductions, an amount equal to: the product of: the Mezzanine Advance Rate as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; and the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; plus the sum of: the balance standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Transaction Account on that date); the balance standing to the credit of the Issuer Collections Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Issuer Collections Account on that date); and the balance standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Pre-Funding Account on that date); less the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date; or on any Monthly Payment Date, any Funding Request Date, any Funding Date and any Purchase Date when a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, without double-counting or double-deductions, an amount equal to: the product of.: the Mezzanine Advance Rate as at the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; and the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance that relates to each Purchased Receivable that has a Purchase Date prior to the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; plus the product of..: the percentage that is equal to: the Mezzanine Advance Rate; less the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage; and the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance that relates to each Purchased Receivable that has a Purchase Date on or following the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; plus the sum of.: the balance standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Transaction Account on that date); the balance standing to the credit of the Issuer Collections Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Issuer Collections Account on that date); and the balance standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Pre-Funding Account on that date); less the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date.

“Mezzanine Commitment” means: in relation to a Mezzanine Note Purchaser as at the Closing Date, the amount set opposite its name under the heading “Mezzanine Commitment” in Schedule 1 (The Mezzanine Note Purchasers) to the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, as that amount may be reduced or increased from time to time in accordance with clause 10 (Reduction or termination of the Mezzanine Commitments) to 11 (Increase of the Mezzanine Commitments) (inclusive) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement; and after the Closing Date, in relation to any other Mezzanine Note Purchaser, the amount of any Mezzanine Commitment (i) transferred or assigned to it or (ii) in respect of which it has agreed to become a Mezzanine Note Purchaser in connection with an increase in the Mezzanine Commitment and, in each case, has executed a Deed of Accession, a Commitment Transfer Certificate, an Assignment Agreement or any other permitted form of transfer or assignment, as the context requires, in accordance with the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, in each case, as evidenced by any updated copy of the table set out at Schedule 1 (The Mezzanine Note Purchasers) to the Mezzanine Facility Agreement delivered by the Servicer from time to time in accordance with clause 14 (Actions following adjustment to MezzanineCommitments) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement.
“Mezzanine Facilities Limit” means, as at any date of determination, the lower of: the Mezzanine Total Commitments; and the Mezzanine Borrowing Base.

“Mezzanine NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Amount” means, as at any date of determination following (and including) the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Applicable Date, the amount equal to the aggregate of: the Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Direct Debit/Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount; the Maximum Average Weighted Remaining Term Excess Concentration Amount; the Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount; the Single Employer Partner Excess Concentration Amount; the Subprime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Top Five Employer Partner Excess Concentration Amount; and the Weighted Average APR Excess Concentration Amount.

Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance: means, on any Business Day, the balance equal to the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables which are Eligible Receivables less (without double counting any Eligible Receivables so its Outstanding Principal Balance is deducted more than once from the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance): an amount equal to the sum of Mezzanine NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Amount; and Unallocated Cash, in each case, on that day, on the understanding that, for the purposes of this definition only, any outstanding cash and credits relating to any Borrower shall be treated as applied to Eligible Receivables of that Borrower, in order from most to least delinquent.
“Mezzanine Note Purchaser Account” means the bank account designated by the Mezzanine Note Purchaser, in writing, from time to time, on reasonable prior notice to the Servicer.
“Mezzanine Note Purchaser Group” means the Mezzanine Note Purchaser and any Affiliate of the Mezzanine Note Purchaser.

“Mezzanine Note Reduction Amount” means, in respect of any reduction of a Mezzanine Note in accordance with any Mezzanine Optional Redemption, the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Note to be redeemed, in whole or in part, together with any accrued interest.

Mezzanine Offer Period: means the period during which a Mezzanine Increase Offer is open for acceptance by the Mezzanine Note Purchasers, as specified in the relevant facility agreement provisions regarding commitment increases.

“Mezzanine Optional Redemption” means any redemption of any amount under any Mezzanine Note in accordance with Mezzanine Note Conditions 4.1 (Optional Redemption by the Issuer) to 4.4 (Optional Redemption by the Mezzanine Note Purchaser) or Mezzanine Note Condition 4.6 (Optional Redemption due to tax).

“Mezzanine Pre-Funding Account Amount” means, the amount to be credited to the Pre-Funding Account Mezzanine Ledger as determined by the Seller and the Servicer and notified to the Cash Manager on any Funding Date, provided that the amount shall not cause the Mezzanine Pre-Funding Limit to be exceeded.
“Mezzanine Pre-Funding Limit” means GBP 1,200,000.

“Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding” means at any date of determination, in respect of any Mezzanine Note, an amount equal to: the initial Mezzanine Subscription Price in respect of the Mezzanine Note; plus the aggregate Mezzanine Subscription Price in respect of any Mezzanine Note which has been paid at any time after the Closing Date and on or before that date; less the sum of: the Mezzanine Redemption Amount which has become due and payable and has been paid on or before that date; any Pre-Funding Mezzanine Redemption Amount that has been satisfied by payment to the Mezzanine Note Purchaser; and the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage Redemption Amount which has become due and payable and has been paid on or before that date, provided that if the amount is reduced by any principal payment which is rescinded or must be otherwise returned for any reason, the amount shall be deemed to be increased by the amount so rescinded or required to be returned with effect from the time at which that payment was made.

“Mezzanine Redemption Amount” means the amount, on any Monthly Payment Date, equal to: if the Revolving Period is continuing (other than in any circumstance described in sub-paragraphs (e) or (f) below), the amount (if any) by which the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Note as at the most recent Funding Date or Monthly Payment Date, as applicable, (after taking account of any anticipated redemptions or Mezzanine Utilisations on the Monthly Payment Date) exceeds the Mezzanine Borrowing Base as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; any Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage Redemption Amount that is payable on that date; if the Revolving Period has ended but prior to the Final Maturity Date (other than in any circumstance described in sub-paragraphs (d), (e) and (f) below), the amount available to redeem the Mezzanine Notes in full (together with any accrued interest) as at the Monthly Payment Date after satisfaction in full of all amounts ranking in priority to payment of principal in respect of the Mezzanine Notes in the applicable Priority of Payments; in respect of the Final Maturity Date or following the occurrence of a Mezzanine Event of Default or any mandatory redemption required under Mezzanine Note Condition 4.11 (Mandatory Redemption on a Mezzanine Event of Default) or Mezzanine Note Condition 4.13 (Mandatory Redemption on occurrence of a Subordinated Event of Default or early redemption of the Subordinated Loan) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Notes (together with any accrued interest and Break Costs, if applicable) as at the Monthly Payment Date; if it is unlawful for any Mezzanine Note Purchaser to continue to participate in the Mezzanine Facilities, unlawful for the Issuer to perform or comply with any of its obligations under a Mezzanine Note or the Transaction Documents or if there is a redemption due to tax, the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the affected Mezzanine Note (together with any accrued interest) as at the Monthly Payment Date; and in respect of any Mezzanine Optional Redemption of the Mezzanine Note, the Mezzanine Note Reduction Amount as at the Monthly Payment Date.
Mezzanine Subscription Price: means, in relation to any Mezzanine Note, the amount requested by the Issuer as such in any Mezzanine Funding Request in respect of that Mezzanine Note.
“Mezzanine Total Commitments” means the aggregate of the Mezzanine Commitments, being GBP 25,000,000 at the date of this Agreement.
“Mezzanine Total Commitments Increase Limit” means GBP 50,000,000.

Mezzanine Transaction: means the specific transaction constituted by the Mezzanine Facility Agreement and the Mezzanine Notes involving the advance of funds by the Mezzanine Note Purchasers to the Issuer.

Mezzanine Unused Additional Interest: means the additional interest or commitment fee payable on the undrawn portion of the Mezzanine Commitments, calculated as a percentage per annum on the daily undrawn amount.
“Mezzanine Utilisation” means the subscription and purchase by a Mezzanine Note Purchaser of a Mezzanine Note under the Mezzanine Facility Agreement.

MiFiD II Regulations: means Directive 2014/65/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on markets in financial instruments (MiFID II) and Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 on markets in financial instruments (MiFIR), together with any delegated or implementing acts and transposition legislation.
“Minimum Excess Spread Amount” means GBP 1.

Minimum Mezzanine Denomination: means the specified minimum principal amount for the Mezzanine Notes, typically established to qualify for exemptions from prospectus requirements or other regulatory thresholds (e.g., GBP 100,000).

Minimum Required Interest: means the material net economic interest in the securitisation which must be retained on an ongoing basis (typically not less than 5 per cent) in accordance with the Securitisation Regulations (risk retention requirements).

“Monthly Investor Report” means the monthly investor report substantially in the forms agreed between the Cash Manager, the Issuer, the Mezzanine Funding Agent and the Facility Agent on or before the Closing Date, being each of the forms set out at (a) Annex XII of the UK Sec Reg Disclosure Standards and (b) Annex XII of the EU Article 7 Technical Standards, in each case as of the Signing Date, or any other form which is agreed between the Cash Manager, the Issuer, the Mezzanine Funding Agent and the Facility Agent from time to time.
“Monthly Investor Reporting Date” means the day falling one Business Day prior to each date as set out in paragraph (a) of the definition of Monthly Payment Date.

“Monthly Payment Date” means: prior to the Termination Date, the 26th day of each calendar month (or if such day is not a Business Day, the immediately succeeding Business Day) and the initial payment date shall be 26 February 2023 (or if such day is not a Business Day, the immediately succeeding Business Day); and on and after the Termination Date (other than a Programme Scheduled Termination Date), where there has been a Servicer Termination Event or an Event of Default, each Business Day selected from time to time by the Facility Agent (it being understood that the Facility Agent may select the Monthly Payment Date to occur as frequently as daily) or, in the absence of any such selection, the date which would be the Monthly Payment Date pursuant to sub-paragraph (a) of this definition.

“Monthly Servicer Report” means the monthly servicer report in the form of the spreadsheet and the formulae used in that spreadsheet, a copy of which has been approved by the Facility Agent and delivered to it on the Signing Date as set out in Part C (Form ofMonthly ServicerReport) of Schedule 3 (Form of Reports) to the Servicing Agreement (which may only be amended by agreement in writing by the Facility Agent, the Security Trustee, the Mezzanine Funding Agent and the Servicer, including with respect to any proposed amendment to any formula contained in the spreadsheet).
“Monthly Servicer Reporting Date” means the day falling three Business Days prior to each Monthly Payment Date as set out in paragraph (a) of the definition of Monthly Payment Date.

“Most Senior Lender Instruction” means: for so long as there is any Senior Commitment outstanding or there is any amount outstanding under the Senior Loans, an instruction from the Majority Senior Lenders; or at any time that paragraph (a) above does not apply and for so long as there is any Mezzanine Commitment outstanding or any amount outstanding under the Mezzanine Notes, an instruction in writing, from the Mezzanine Note Purchasers whose total commitments to provide Mezzanine Facilities under the Mezzanine Facility Agreement are in aggregate at least equal to 66⅔ per cent. of the Mezzanine Total Commitments (or, if the Mezzanine Commitments are no longer outstanding, at least equal to 66⅔ per cent. of the Mezzanine Principal Amounts Outstanding), provided that, in respect of any Basic Term Modification, the Facility Agent shall be bound by the terms of Clause 3.19 (Basic Term Modification) of the Master Framework Agreement.

“Most Senior Lenders” means: for so long as there is any Senior Commitment outstanding or there is any amount outstanding under the Senior Loans, the Majority Senior Lenders; at any time that paragraph (a) does not apply, and for so long as there is any Mezzanine Commitment outstanding, there is any Mezzanine Note outstanding or the total commitments to provide Mezzanine Facilities under the Mezzanine Facility Agreement are greater than zero, the Mezzanine Note Purchasers; and at any time that paragraph (a) and (b) do not apply, the Subordinated Lender.

“Near Prime Borrower” means a Borrower that, for the purposes of the Seller’s underwriting and completion of a responsible lending assessment in respect of that Borrower, has obtained: a Gauge 2 Score of at least 551 and no more than 590; and a Delphi 11SBN Score of at least 611 and no more than 790.
Near Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage: means the maximum percentage of the Portfolio designated for Near Prime Borrowers, as specified in the Concentration Limits schedule.

Near Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the amount by which the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Receivables owed by Near Prime Borrowers exceeds the Near Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage.

“Near Prime Excess Concentration Advance Rate Reduction Limit” means, as at any date of determination following the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Applicable Date, an amount equal to the product of: the percentage by which 50.00 per cent. exceeds the Subprime Borrower Advance Rate Percentage as at that date (expressed as a decimal fraction); and the Net Eligible Receivables Balance as at that date.
“Near Prime Receivable” means a Purchased Receivable in respect of which the Borrower is a Near Prime Borrower.

“Near Prime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount” means, as at any date of determination, the amount by which: the aggregate of the Outstanding Principal Balances of all Near Prime Receivables as at that date (excluding any Near Prime Receivables falling within the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Amount); exceeds the Near Prime Excess Concentration Advance Rate Reduction Limit, as at that date.

“NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Applicable Date” means the Monthly Payment Date on which the aggregate of the Outstanding Principal Balances of all Purchased Receivables on their respective Purchase Date is first greater than GBP 25,000,000.
“Net Eligible Receivables Balance” means, as applicable: the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance; or the Senior Net Eligible Receivables Balance.

“Net Excess Spread Amount” means, with respect to any Monthly Payment Date by reference to the Monthly Investor Report in respect of that Monthly Payment Date, the amount of Available Distribution Amount remaining after giving effect to all payments set out in paragraphs 1 to 19 of the Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments.

New Programme Scheduled Termination Date: means the new scheduled date for the termination of the programme established pursuant to an extension request in accordance with the Master Framework Agreement.
New Senior Lender: means a person to whom an existing Senior Lender assigns or transfers any of its rights and obligations under the Senior Facility Agreement.
“Northern Irish Borrower” means any Borrower that, at the time that they enter into a Borrower Agreement, is resident in Northern Ireland.

“Northern Irish Receivable Recharacterisation Event” means any judgment, decree, declaration, decision or order (whether interim or final) of any supervisory authority, tribunal, court or other governmental authority that requires any Receivable originated by the Seller or other unsecured personal loan (whether originated by [PARTY_NAME] or any other party) entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Northern Ireland, to be subject to, or otherwise construed in accordance with, Northern Irish law (in whole or in part) in accordance with overriding mandatory provisions of Northern Irish law, rather than the law which the Receivable or unsecured personal loan is expressed to be governed in accordance with its contractual terms.
“Northern Irish Receivables” means Receivables which derive from Borrower Agreements that are governed by, subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Northern Irish law.

“Notice of Collections Account Declaration of Trust” means the notice from the Seller to the Collections Account Bank relating to the Collections Account Declaration of Trust substantially in the form set out in Schedule 1 (Notice of Declaration of Trust) to the Collections Account Declaration of Trust.
“Notice of Security” means a notice of security in form and substance satisfactory to the Facility Agent and the Security Trustee.
Offer: means an offer to sell Receivables and their Related Rights made by the Seller to the Issuer (or Purchaser) pursuant to the terms of the Receivables Purchase Agreement.
Offer Date: means the date on which an Offer to sell Receivables is made by the Seller to the Issuer.
Optional Repayment Notice: means a notice delivered by the Issuer to the Facility Agent indicating the Issuer's intention to make a voluntary repayment of the Senior Loan.
“Original Mezzanine Funding Agent” means each persons who is a Mezzanine Funding Agent on the Closing Date.
“Original Mezzanine Note Purchaser” means each person who is a Mezzanine Note Purchaser on the Closing Date.
Original Programme Scheduled Termination Date: means the initial scheduled termination date of the programme as agreed on the Closing Date, prior to any extension.

“Original Senior Lender Group” means the Original Senior Lender and any of its Affiliates, Related Funds and any conduit purchaser entity that it administers or is administered by an Affiliate or Related Fund of the Original Senior Lender.
“Origination Date” means the date on which a Receivable is originated.
“Outstanding Principal Balance” means, in respect of any Receivable, as at any date of determination, the unpaid principal amounts due in respect of it from the relevant Borrower as at that date.
“Paying Transaction Party” means, where any party is under an obligation created by a Transaction Document to make a payment to a Receiving Transaction Party, the party who is to make such payment.

“Perfection Event” means any Early Amortisation Event, other than: any event occurring under paragraph 1(a) (Performance Ratios/Triggers) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; any event occurring under paragraph 1(b) (Payment not by Salary Deduction) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; any event occurring under paragraph 1(c) (Senior Borrowing Base) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; any event occurring under paragraph 1(d) (Cash Reserve) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement as a result of the Cash Reserve being less than the Cash Reserve Target Amount on any Monthly Payment Date, solely on account of there not being sufficient Available Distribution Amount on that date to replenish the Cash Reserve pursuant to the relevant Priority of Payments, rather than any failure to fund the Cash Reserve from the proceeds of any Subordinated Advance in connection with an increase to the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding; on any date from and including the date that is six months from the Closing Date, any event occurring under paragraph 1(e) (Excess Spread) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; any event occurring under paragraph 1(f) (Senior Borrowing Base) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; any event occurring under paragraph 6(e) (Change of Control) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement; or any event occurring under paragraph 8(c) (Issuer Account Bank Event) of Schedule 4 (Early Amortisation Events) to the Master Framework Agreement.

“Permitted Modification” means any amendment or modification: which is of a minor or technical nature or to correct a manifest error; required to comply with any law, regulation or rules and guidance from the FCA, ICO or other regulator or any trade body applicable to the Sellers from time to time; which imposes tighter or more conservative credit criteria and is otherwise not adverse in any respect to the interests of the Funders; made with the consent of the Facility Agent (acting on the instructions of each Senior Lender and each Mezzanine Funding Agent) and the Security Trustee (acting on the instructions of the Instructing Creditor) (not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed); or that is a Receivable Payment Date Change, provided that any amendments or modifications requested by [PARTY_NAME] and approved by Latham & Watkins LLP on or prior to the Closing Date shall constitute Permitted Modifications.

“Permitted Transferee” means any Affiliate of the Senior Lender provided that, following such transfer or assignment, the Issuer will not be required by law to make any withholding or deduction from any amounts payable to the transferee or assignee in respect of the Senior Facility or otherwise to pay increased costs in accordance with the increased costs indemnity.
Portfolio Trustee: means the trustee appointed to hold the trust over the Receivables and related rights pursuant to the Declaration of Trust.

Post-Enforcement Priority of Payments: means the order of priority of payments to be applied by the Security Trustee in respect of monies received or recovered following the enforcement of the Transaction Security.

“Potential Early Amortisation Event” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute an Early Amortisation Event.
