“Potential Investor” means any potential transferee of a Senior Commitment or Mezzanine Note that has complied with the requirements of Clause 24 (Confidentiality) of the Master Framework Agreement and would satisfy any transfer restrictions in the Transaction Documents.

“Potential Mezzanine Event of Default” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute a Mezzanine Event of Default.

“Potential Servicer Termination Event” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute a Servicer Termination Event.

Pre‑Enforcement Priority of Payments: means the order of priority in which payments are to be made by the Issuer using Available Revenue Receipts and Available Principal Receipts prior to the delivery of an Enforcement Notice, typically prioritizing taxes, fees, and senior interest before principal payments and subordinated amounts.

“Pre-Funding Account” means any pre-funding account in the name of the Issuer designated in writing by the Seller, Issuer and the Facility Agent, from time to time, to fall within this definition and maintained at all times at an Account Bank Eligible Institution.
“Pre-Funding Account Mezzanine Ledger” means the ledger in the Pre-Funding Account to which the Mezzanine Pre-Funding Account Amount is credited.
“Pre-Funding Limit” means the amount that is equal to the aggregate of the Senior Pre-Funding Limit and the Mezzanine Pre-Funding Limit.

Pre-Funding Mezzanine Redemption Amount: means any amount standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account Mezzanine Ledger at the end of the Pre-Funding Period (or such other specified date) which has not been utilized to purchase Receivables, to be repaid to the Mezzanine Note Purchasers.

Pre-Funding Senior Repayment Amount: means any amount standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account Senior Ledger at the end of the Pre-Funding Period (or such other specified date) which has not been utilized to purchase Receivables, to be repaid to the Senior Lenders.

“Principal Amount Outstanding” means as at any date of determination: in respect of the Senior Facility, the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding; and in respect of any Mezzanine Note, the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding.
Priority of Payments: means the Pre‑Enforcement Priority of Payments or, as applicable, the Post‑Enforcement Priority of Payments.

“Pro Rata Share” means: for any Senior Lender: the Senior Commitment of such Senior Lender, divided by the Senior Total Commitments; and after the Senior Total Commitments have been reduced to zero, the Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding funded by such Senior Lender, divided by the aggregate Senior Principal Amount Outstanding of the Senior Loans funded by all Senior Lenders; and for any Mezzanine Note Purchaser: the Mezzanine Commitment of such Mezzanine Note Purchaser, divided by the Mezzanine Total Commitments; and after the Mezzanine Total Commitments have been reduced to zero, the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Notes funded by such Mezzanine Note Purchaser, divided by the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Notes funded by all Mezzanine Note Purchasers.

“Programme Scheduled Termination Date” means the later of: if, at any time prior to the date falling one year after the Closing Date, the Original Senior Lender delivers notice in writing to the Seller that the “Programme Scheduled Termination Date” is the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 24 months after the Closing Date, the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 24 months after the Closing Date; if no notice is delivered in accordance with paragraph (a) above, the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 36 months after the Closing Date; or any other Monthly Payment Date agreed between the parties in writing, from time to time, in accordance with Clause 3.5 (Extension of the Programme Scheduled Termination Date) of the Master Framework Agreement.

“Purchase Date” means, in respect of any Receivable, any calendar day occurring in the Revolving Period on which the relevant Seller wishes to sell the Receivable to the Issuer in accordance with the terms of the Receivables Purchase Agreement, or as the context requires, the Business Day on which the Issuer has purchased the Receivable from the relevant Seller.

“Purchase Date Condition” means, in respect of any Business Day during the Revolving Period that the Servicer wishes to deem a Purchase Date, the condition that must be satisfied on that date, being that a duly completed List of Receivables has been delivered by the relevant Seller to the Issuer and the Facility Agent on that date, recording the Receivables in respect of which Initial Purchase Price has been paid on that Purchase Date that is also a Subordinated Settlement Date (or otherwise payment of Initial Purchase Price is to be paid by way of Subordinated Advances made in accordance with the Subordinated Facilities Agreement).
Purchase Price: means, in respect of each Receivable, its Initial Purchase Price.

“Purchased Receivable” means, as at any date of determination, any Receivable which has been purchased (or purported to have been purchased) by the Issuer that remains outstanding at that time and which has not been repurchased or re-transferred by the Seller in accordance with the terms of the Transaction Documents.
“Push Payment” means any payment that is: made manually by a Borrower; or made by a third party (other than an Employer Partner) in the context of an IVA or a debt management plan.

Push Payments Concentration Percentage: means the maximum permitted percentage of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that may be comprised of Receivables where the Borrowers make payments via Push Payments (manual or third-party payments).

Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount: means the portion of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables associated with Push Payments that exceeds the Push Payments Concentration Percentage limit.

“Qualifying Senior Lender” means a Senior Lender that is: beneficially entitled to interest payable to that Senior Lender in respect of the relevant Senior Advance and is: a Senior Lender which is (or was at the time the relevant Senior Advance was made) a bank (as defined for the purpose of section 879 of the ITA) and is within the charge to United Kingdom corporation tax in respect of any payments of interest made in respect of that Senior Advance (or would be within such charge in respect of such payments but for section 18A of the CTA); a Senior Lender which is: a company resident in the United Kingdom for United Kingdom tax purposes; a company not so resident in the United Kingdom but which carries on a trade in the United Kingdom through a permanent establishment and the whole of any interest payable in respect of that Senior Advance falls to be brought into account in computing its chargeable profits (within the meaning of section 19 of the CTA) by reason of Part 17 of the CTA; or a partnership, each member of which is a person falling within (A) or (B) above or a person or body mentioned in section 936 of the ITA; a Treaty Senior Lender; or a building society (as defined for the purpose of section 880 of the ITA) making a Senior Advance.

“Receivable” means all amounts owing by a Borrower, present and future, absolute or contingent, due now or in the future (including, without limitation, any Finance Charges), from time to time, arising under a Borrower Agreement in respect of a Consumer Loan to a Borrower in the United Kingdom.

“Receivable Payment Date Change” means, in respect of any Receivable and its related Consumer Loan, a change of the calendar date on which the scheduled instalment payment date occurs in accordance with the terms of the Borrower Agreement: to correct an operational, administrative or technical issue raised by the Employer or the Servicer; where the Employer restructures payroll; at the request of the Borrower, provided that: the Employee makes the request as a result of a termination of their employment with the Employer Partner; the relevant Consumer Loan is not in arrears; and the requested amended payment date is within 15 calendar days of the previously scheduled payment date; or to implement payment holidays that are provided in accordance with FCA industry guidance.
“Receivables Purchase Agreement” means the receivables purchase agreement, dated on or about the Signing Date between the Issuer, the Security Trustee, the Sellers and the Facility Agent.

“Reduced Rate of Return” means the amount (if any) by which: the interest which a Senior Lender or a Mezzanine Note Purchaser should have received for the period from the date of receipt of all or any part of its Senior Commitments, Mezzanine Commitments or Unpaid Sum (as applicable) to the last day of the current Interest Period in respect of that Senior Commitment, Mezzanine Commitment or Unpaid Sum, had the principal amount or Unpaid Sum received been paid on the last day of that Interest Period; exceeds: the amount which that Senior Lender or that Mezzanine Note Purchaser would be able to obtain by placing an amount equal to the principal amount or Unpaid Sum received by it on deposit with a leading bank in the Relevant Interbank Market for a period starting on the Business Day following receipt or recovery and ending on the last day of the current Interest Period.

“Related Rights” means, in respect of any Receivable: all deposits, guarantees, rights under any insurance policy written for the benefit of the Seller, indemnities, warranties and other agreements or arrangements of whatever character from time to time supporting or securing payment of that Receivable, to the extent transferable in accordance with their terms and under applicable law without the consent of any party other than the Seller; all rights to receive and obtain payment under the Borrower Agreement and/or the Employer Partner Service Agreement relating to the Receivable (including, without limitation, any right to demand, sue for, recover, receive and give receipts for payment of any amount or any other right to enforce against the relevant Borrower or an Employer Partner in so far as it relates to the Receivable); any contractual rights the Seller may have to enforce, or giving rise to a cause of action in respect of, any Purchased Receivable, which may exist as at the origination date of the Borrower Agreement or at any time in the future; any contractual rights, or cause of action, the Seller may have against an Employer Partner under an Employer Partner Service Agreement in so for as it relates to the Receivable and any proceeds relating to the Receivable received from the Employer Partner (including, without limitation, any recoveries from default interest and losses corresponding to the Receivable); and all proceeds (including, any Collections), however arising, of the payment or repayment, sale or other disposal (including for debt management purposes) or enforcement of, or dealing with, decree or judgment relating to the Receivable and any pledge, retention of title or other security for its payment.

Repurchase Price: means: (a) in respect of any Purchased Receivable that is a Defaulted Receivable and is repurchased by the Seller for the purpose of on-selling such Purchased Receivable, the purchase price paid by such third party to purchase the Receivable from the Seller; or (b) in respect of any other Purchased Receivable, an amount equal to its Outstanding Principal Balance, plus any accrued and unpaid interest and fees as at that date and any costs and expenses incurred by the Issuer as a result of the repurchase.
“Revolving Period” means the period from (and including) the Closing Date to (but excluding) the Termination Date.

“Salary Deduction” means the deductions made from, or adjustments made to, the salary of an Employee for the purpose of the repayment of the Consumer Loan advanced by the Seller to that Employee in accordance with the relevant instruction file.

“Scottish Assignation in Security” means each assignation in security governed by Scots law made between the Issuer, the Security Trustee and the Seller and granted pursuant to clause 4.5 (Scottish Receivables) of the Security Agreement and substantially in the form set out in schedule 2 (Form of Scottish Assignation in Security) to the Security Agreement.

“Scottish Declaration of Trust” means each Scottish Declaration of Trust granted by the Seller in favour of the Issuer pursuant to clause 2.6 or clause 2.7 (Scottish Declarations of Trust) of the Receivables Purchase Agreement and in substantially the form annexed in Schedule 2 (Form of Scottish Declaration of Trust) to the Receivables Purchase Agreement.

“Scottish Receivable Recharacterisation Event” means: any judgment, decree, declaration, decision or order (whether interim or final) of any supervisory authority, tribunal, court or other governmental authority that requires any Receivable originated by the Seller or other unsecured personal loan (whether originated by [PARTY_NAME] or any other party) entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Scotland, to be subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law (in whole or in part) in accordance with overriding mandatory provisions of Scots law or any other relevant provisions of Scots law, rather than the law which the Receivable or unsecured personal loan is expressed to be governed in accordance with its contractual terms; or a determination by the Facility Agent (acting on the instructions of the Most Senior Lenders (acting reasonably)), that any Purchased Receivable which has been entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Scotland should be treated as being subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law (in whole or in part), rather than the law which the Purchased Receivable is expressed to be governed by in accordance with its contractual terms, on the basis that such determination is necessary for the protection of the interests of the Issuer or any of the Secured Creditors in the Purchased Receivables.
“Scottish Receivables” means Receivables which derive from Borrower Agreements that are governed by, subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law.

“Scottish Trust” means the Scots law trust created pursuant to a Scottish Declaration of Trust in respect of Scottish Receivables which are Purchased Receivables granted pursuant to the procedures referred to in the Receivables Purchase Agreement.

“Secured Creditors” means the Senior Lenders, the Mezzanine Note Purchasers, the Mezzanine Funding Agents, the Subordinated Lenders, any Appointee or Receiver appointed pursuant to the Security Agreement, the Facility Agent, the Cash Manager, the Security Trustee, Servicer, Seller, Collections Account Trustee and Subordinated Lender (in its capacities as the Seller and Servicer), the Swap Provider, the Corporate Services Provider, the Share Trustee, the Issuer Account Bank and the Registrar.
“Senior Advance” means any advance of a Senior Loan made by the Senior Lenders pursuant to the terms of the Senior Facility Agreement.

“Senior Advance Rate” means, as at any date of determination, the percentage equal to: the weighted average percentage that is calculated by applying the following, as relevant: 84.50 per cent. for the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Eligible Receivables, excluding any Receivables falling within the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount or Near Prime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; 60.00 per cent. for the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; and 77.50 per cent. for the Near Prime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount, in each case, as at that date; or any other percentage agreed in writing between the Senior Lenders and the Seller from time to time.

“Senior Advance Rate Reduction Event” means, as at any Determination Date, any of the following events: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding in respect of Borrowers that are paying by way of direct debit or Push Payments for at least two consecutive calendar months ending on that Determination Date (rather than by way of Salary Deduction), excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been outstanding for more than 90 days, is greater than 19.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables as at that Determination Date, excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been outstanding for more than 90 days; or the Default Rate during the most recent consecutive three-month period ending on the Determination Date, is greater than 1.25 per cent. as calculated on that Determination Date, provided that, in respect of paragraphs (a) and/or (b) above, where the relevant breach, or breaches, has, or have, been remedied and no further breach has occurred for at least three consecutive Determination Dates, no reduction to the Senior Advance Rate shall apply (and no waiver in this respect shall be required).
“Senior Available Commitments” means, at any time, the amount equal to: the Senior Facility Limit; less the aggregate Principal Amount Outstanding under the Senior Facility at that time.

“Senior Commitment” means: in relation to the Original Senior Lender, the amount set opposite its name at such applicable times under the heading “Commitment” in Schedule 1 (The Senior Lenders) to the Senior Facility Agreement (as amended and restated from time to time), as that amount may be increased or reduced from time to time in accordance with clause 2.2 (Adjustment to the Senior Total Commitments) of the Senior Facility Agreement; and in relation to any other Senior Lender, the amount of any Senior Commitment transferred to it under the Senior Facility Agreement or otherwise, the amount set opposite its name under the heading “Commitment” in schedule 1 (The Senior Lenders) to the Senior Facility Agreement (as amended and restated from time to time), in each case, as evidenced by any updated copy of the table set out at Schedule 1 (The Senior Lenders) to the Senior Facility Agreement delivered by the Servicer from time to time in accordance with clause 2.5(b) (Calculation of Pro Rata Shares following adjustment to the Senior Commitments) of the Senior Facility Agreement.
“Senior Facility” means the revolving loan facility made available under the Senior Facility Agreement as described in clause 2 (The Facility and purpose) of the Senior Facility Agreement.
“Senior Facility Limit” means, as at any date of determination, the lower of: the Senior Total Commitments; and the Senior Borrowing Base.

“Senior Lender Buyout Amount” means, in respect of a Senior Lender, an amount equal to the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding at the time of purchase, together with any accrued and unpaid fees, expenses (including the reimbursement of professional and legal fees), any indemnity payments, any interest (including any accrued but unpaid interest, but excluding any Senior Cancellation Payment Amount) and any other amounts which have accrued, are reasonably foreseeable or are due and payable to the relevant Senior Lender whatsoever pursuant to the Transaction Documents.

Senior NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Amount: means, as at any date of determination, following (and including) the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Applicable Date, the amount equal to the aggregate of: the Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Direct Debit/Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount; the Maximum Average Weighted Remaining Term Excess Concentration Amount; the Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount; the Single Employer Partner Excess Concentration Amount; the Subprime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount; the Subprime Borrowers/Near Prime Borrowers (Senior) Excess Concentration Amount; the Top Five Employer Partner Excess Concentration Amount; and the Weighted Average APR Excess Concentration Amount.

“Senior Pre-Funding Account Amount” means, the amount to be credited to the Pre-Funding Account Senior Ledger determined by the Seller and the Servicer and notified to the Cash Manager on any Funding Date, provided that the amount shall not cause the Senior Pre-Funding Limit to be exceeded.

“Senior Principal Amount Outstanding” means, as at any date of determination, in respect of any Senior Loan provided by a Senior Lender under the Senior Facility, an amount equal to: the initial Senior Advance under the Senior Loan; plus the aggregate additional Senior Advances made under the Senior Loan at any time after the Closing Date and on or before that date; less the sum of: the Senior Repayment Amount which has become due and payable and has been paid on or before that date; any Pre-Funding Senior Repayment Amount that has been satisfied by payment to the Senior Lender; and the Senior Advance Rate Reduction Percentage Repayment Amount which has become due and payable and has been paid on or before that date, provided that, if the amount is reduced by any principal payment which is rescinded or must be otherwise returned for any reason, the amount shall be deemed to be increased by the amount so rescinded or required to be returned with effect from the time at which that payment was made.

“Senior Reduction Amount” means, in respect of any reduction of a Senior Loan in accordance with a Senior Voluntary Prepayment, the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding to be prepaid, in whole or in part, together with any accrued interest.

“Senior Repayment Amount” means the amount, on any Monthly Payment Date, equal to: if the Revolving Period is continuing (other than in any circumstance described in sub-paragraphs (d) or (e) below), the amount (if any) by which the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date (after taking account of any anticipated repayments of Senior Advances on the Monthly Payment Date) exceeds the Senior Borrowing Base as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; or if the Termination Date has occurred but prior to the Final Maturity Date (other than in any circumstance described in sub-paragraphs (c), (d) and (e) below), the amount available to redeem the Senior Loans in full (together with any accrued interest) as at the Monthly Payment Date after satisfaction in full of all amounts ranking in priority to payment of principal in respect of the Senior Facility in the applicable Priority of Payments; in respect of the Final Maturity Date or following the occurrence of an Event of Default or any mandatory redemption required under clause 7.8 (Mandatory repayment following the occurrence of a Mezzanine Event of Default, Subordinated Event of Default, early redemption of the Mezzanine Note or early repayment of the Subordinated Loan) of the Senior Facility Agreement, the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding (together with any accrued interest and Break Costs, if applicable) as at the Monthly Payment Date; if it is unlawful for any Senior Lender to continue to participate in the Senior Loan, unlawful for the Issuer to perform or comply with any of its obligations under the Senior Facility or the Transaction Documents, or if there is a redemption due to tax, the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding (together with any accrued interest) as at the Monthly Payment Date; and in respect of any Senior Voluntary Prepayment, the Senior Reduction Amount as at the Monthly Payment Date.

“Senior Total Commitments” means the aggregate of the Senior Commitments, which may be increased or decreased from time to time in accordance with clause 2.2 (Increase to the Senior Total Commitments) of the Senior Facility Agreement;

“Senior Total Commitments Available Amount” means, in respect of any Senior Total Commitments Increase as at any date of determination, an amount equal to: the Senior Total Commitments Increase Limit as at that date; minus the Senior Total Commitments on that date.
Senior Utilisation: means the advance by a Senior Lender of a Senior Advance under the Senior Facility Agreement.

Senior Utilisation Date: means, the date determined, as follows: in respect of the first Senior Utilisation Request delivered on the Signing Date, the Closing Date; in respect of any Senior Utilisation Request delivered on the Business Day prior to the Monthly Investor Reporting Date, the immediately succeeding Monthly Payment Date; and in respect of any Senior Utilisation Request delivered on any calendar date during the Revolving Period, the Weekly Utilisation Date, in each case, provided that the relevant Conditions Precedent to Utilisation in respect of that date have been satisfied in full.

Senior Voluntary Prepayment: means any voluntary prepayment or cancellation of the Senior Facilities made by the Issuer in accordance with the terms of the Senior Facility Agreement, typically requiring prior notice and subject to the payment of any applicable break costs or fees.
“Subordinated Advance” means any advance made by the Subordinated Lenders pursuant to the terms of the Subordinated Facility Agreement.

Subordinated Facility: means the subordinated revolving loan facility granted by the Subordinated Lenders to the Issuer pursuant to the Subordinated Facility Agreement, which ranks junior to the Senior Facility and Mezzanine Facility in the application of funds.

Subordinated Further Utilisation: means a utilisation under the Subordinated Facility made subsequent to the initial utilisation, in accordance with the manual utilisation request procedures set out in the Subordinated Facility Agreement.

Subordinated Lender Repayment Amount: means the amount on any Monthly Payment Date, equal to the lower of: the Subordinated Principal Amount Outstanding on that date (prior to taking account of any redemptions that day); and an amount equal to: if an Early Amortisation Event has not occurred on or prior to that date, the amount by which the Subordinated Principal Amount Outstanding as at the most recent Cut-Off Date exceeds an amount equal to: the sum of: aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; the amount standing to the credit of the Issuer Accounts; and any Agreed Adjusted Ad Hoc Funding Amounts, in each case, as at the most recent Cut-Off Date; less the sum of: the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding on that Monthly Payment Date (after taking account of any further Senior Advances or repayments that day); the aggregate Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding on that Monthly Payment Date (after taking account of any further subscriptions or redemptions that day); and the Agreed Adjusted Ad Hoc Funding Amounts less the Minimum Excess Spread Amount, provided that, in no circumstances shall the application of the amount calculated pursuant to this sub-paragraph result in a breach of the general undertaking in the Securitisation Regulations; or if an Early Amortisation Event has occurred on or prior to that date, an amount equal to: until the Senior Facility and the Mezzanine Notes have been repaid and redeemed in full, zero; and after the Senior Facility and the Mezzanine Notes have been repaid and redeemed in full, all Available Distribution Amounts available to be applied in accordance with the Priority of Payments; or on any Subordinated Settlement Date, the Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount.

“Subordinated Principal Amount Outstanding” means, as at any date of determination, in respect of the Subordinated Facility, an amount equal to: the initial Subordinated Advance under the Subordinated Facility Agreement; plus the aggregate additional Subordinated Advances made under the Subordinated Facility Agreement at any time after the Closing Date and on or before that date; less any amount which has been applied in repayment of the Subordinated Facility on or before that date, provided that, if the amount is reduced by any principal payment which is rescinded or must be otherwise returned for any reason, the amount shall be deemed to be increased by the amount so rescinded or required to be returned with effect from the time at which that payment was made.

“Subordinated Settlement Date” means any date on which the Issuer redeems the Subordinated Loan, in part, by an amount equal to the aggregate Initial Purchase Price paid by the Issuer since the immediately preceding Subordinated Settlement Date or Monthly Payment Date, whichever occurred most recently, solely by way of advances under the Subordinated Loan.

“Subordinated Settlement Date Conditions” means, in respect of any Business Day during the Revolving Period that the Servicer wishes to deem a Subordinated Settlement Date, the conditions that must be satisfied on that date, as follows: other than the initial Subordinated Settlement Date in the Revolving Period, the proposed Subordinated Settlement Date must not occur in the period between a Monthly Servicer Reporting Date (exclusive) to but excluding a Monthly Payment Date; no Early Amortisation Event has occurred and is continuing as at that date (without taking account of any remedy or cure period at that time), unless waived in accordance with Clause 3.28 (Waiver of Servicer Termination Event, Early Amortisation Event, Event of Default or Mezzanine Event of Default) of the Master Framework Agreement; a duly completed Borrowing Base Report is delivered to the Facility Agent on that date in accordance with clauses 6.1 and 6.2 (Borrowing Base Report) of the Servicing Agreement, recording compliance with the Senior Borrowing Base and the Mezzanine Borrowing Base on that Subordinated Settlement Date (after taking account of any increase or decrease to the aggregate Principal Amount Outstanding of the Senior Facility and the Mezzanine Notes that day); and on any Subordinated Settlement Date, any withdrawal from any Issuer Account (other than the Pre-Funding Account) for the purpose of paying the Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount to the Subordinated Lender, shall not cause the Issuer to have an Available Distribution Amount which is insufficient to pay amounts due and payable at paragraphs (1) to (19) (inclusive) of the Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments on the next Monthly Payment Date.

“Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount” means, on any Subordinated Settlement Date, the amount equal to the difference between: the Subordinated Advances that have been applied towards the payment of Initial Purchase Price; and the product of: the amount equal to: the Mezzanine Advance Rate on that date; less if a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, any relevant Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage, and the Subordinated Advances that have been applied towards the payment of Initial Purchase Price; in each case, since the later of: the prior Subordinated Settlement Date; and the most recent Monthly Payment Date.
“Subordinated Utilisation Date” means the Closing Date, any Funding Date and any Business Day on which funding is required to purchase Receivables.

Subprime Advance Rate Reduction Limit: means the specified percentage of the Senior Net Eligible Receivables Balance (e.g., 8.0 per cent) which acts as a threshold for determining advance rate reductions related to subprime concentrations.

“Subprime Borrower” means a Borrower that, for the purposes of the Seller’s underwriting and completion of a responsible lending assessment in respect of that Borrower, has obtained: a Gauge 2 Score of no more than 550; and a Delphi 11SBN Score of no more than 610.

“Subprime Borrower Advance Rate Percentage” means the percentage of the Senior Net Eligible Receivables Balance that is comprised of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Subprime Borrowers.

Subprime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the amount by which the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables owing by Subprime Borrowers exceeds the Subprime Borrowers Concentration Limit.

Subprime Borrowers/Near Prime Borrowers (Senior) Concentration Percentage: means the percentage of the Total Receivables Balance comprised of Receivables owing by Subprime Borrowers and Near Prime Borrowers, calculated for the purpose of testing the Senior Facility concentration limits.

Subprime Borrowers/Near Prime Borrowers (Senior) Excess Concentration Amount: means the amount by which the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Receivables owing by Subprime Borrowers and Near Prime Borrowers exceeds the applicable concentration limit for the Senior Facility.
“Subprime Receivable” means a Purchased Receivable in respect of which the Borrower is a Subprime Borrower.

“Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount” means, as at any date of determination following the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Applicable Date, the amount by which: (a) the aggregate of the Outstanding Principal Balances of all Subprime Receivables (excluding any Subprime Receivables falling within the NERB Aggregate Excess Concentration Amount); exceeds (b) the Subprime Advance Rate Reduction Limit, in each case, as at that date.
Subscription Price: means the Senior Utilisation Amount, Mezzanine Subscription Price or Subordinated Subscription Price, as the context requires.
“Successor Cash Manager” means an entity identified and appointed to act as successor Cash Manager in accordance with the Cash Management Agreement to perform the cash management services.

Successor Servicer: means an entity appointed to act as the successor to the Servicer following a Servicer Termination Event or resignation of the Servicer, in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement.

“Swap Agreement” means any agreement entered into between the Swap Provider and the Issuer in connection with the Transaction for the purpose of hedging the Issuer’s exposure to certain interest rate risk, designated in writing at any time by the Facility Agent, the Issuer and the Security Trustee to fall within this definition, which shall include all Hedging Transactions entered into and governed by such agreement.
“Swap Agreement Effective Date” means the date upon which the Swap Provider and the Issuer enter into a Swap Agreement.

“Swap Provider” means, upon accession by such person to the Master Framework Agreement in accordance with Clause 3.47 (Accession of a new or successor Swap Provider): (a) Swap Provider; or (b) any other person that, with the consent of the Facility Agent (acting on a Most Senior Lender Instruction) enters into a Swap Agreement or is a transferee in respect of an existing Swap Agreement.
“Swap Rate” means, at any time, the fixed interest rate payable under the Swap Agreement.

“Swap Subordinated Amounts” means any termination amount due from the Issuer to the Swap Provider arising out of an Event of Default (as defined in the Swap Agreement) where the Swap Provider is the Defaulting Party (as defined in the Swap Agreement).

“Swap Tax Credits” means any credit, allowance, set-off or repayment received by the Issuer in respect of Tax from the tax authorities of any jurisdiction relating to any deduction or withholding, giving rise to an increased payment by a Swap Provider to the Issuer under the terms of the relevant Swap Agreement, which for the avoidance of doubt shall not comprise part of the Available Distribution Amounts.
“Swap Termination Amount” means any amount received from the Swap Provider by the Issuer upon early termination of a Hedging Transaction under the Swap Agreement.

“Sweep Account” means the account held in the name of Servicer, Seller, Collections Account Trustee and Subordinated Lender with the Collections Account Bank listed in Part 2 (Collections Accounts) of Schedule 4 (Collections Accounts and Sweep Account) to the Servicing Agreement or any other account in the name of Servicer, Seller, Collections Account Trustee and Subordinated Lender designated in writing by the Seller, the Issuer, the Facility Agent, the Senior Lenders and the Mezzanine Funding Agents, from time to time, to fall within this definition and maintained at all times at an Account Bank Eligible Institution.

Tangible Net Worth: means, in respect of a relevant entity, as at the relevant date of determination and each as determined in accordance with the Accounting Principles and reported in such entity's most recent audited financial statements or periodic management accounts, an amount equal to the sum of (without double counting): (a) the aggregate value of the book equity of the entity and its consolidated subsidiaries (which, for the avoidance of doubt, shall not give credit to any intangible assets); (b) the principal amount outstanding and any accrued interest of any loans advanced to the entity by its parent or shareholders; (c) the principal amount outstanding and any accrued interest of any other shareholder loans; (d) any subordinated debt issued by the Issuer under the Subordinated Facility Agreement with a maturity past or concurrent with the Final Maturity Date; (e) any deferred revenue; and (f) any undrawn amount under any committed facility provided by any shareholder or any other member of the Group that may be applied towards general corporate purposes which is unconditional and may not be cancelled by the lender.

“Termination Date” means the earlier of: (a) the Programme Scheduled Termination Date; (b) the Senior Cancellation Date; and (c) the date on which any Early Amortisation Event occurs and is continuing, unless such Early Amortisation Event is waived by the Facility Agent in accordance with the Transaction Documents.

“Third Party Mezzanine Note Purchaser” means any person (other than an existing Mezzanine Note Purchaser) to whom a Mezzanine Note Purchaser may transfer all or any part of its Mezzanine Commitments under, in respect of and in accordance with the Mezzanine Facility Agreement or a person who becomes a Mezzanine Note Purchaser pursuant to and subject to the restrictions of clause 12 (Increase of the Mezzanine Commitments) and clause 13 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement.

“Third Party Senior Lender” means any person (other than an existing Senior Lender) to whom a Senior Lender may transfer all or any part of its Senior Commitments under, in respect of and in accordance with the Senior Facility Agreement or a person who becomes a third party Senior Lender pursuant to and subject to the restrictions of clause 18 (Assignment and Transfer) of the Senior Facility Agreement.
“Top Five Employer Partner” means ,at any time, the five Employer Partners to which the greatest aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables relates.
Top Five Employer Partner Concentration Percentage: means the percentage of the Total Receivables Balance represented by Purchased Receivables which relate to the Top Five Employer Partners.

Top Five Employer Partner Excess Concentration Amount: means the amount by which the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables relating to the Top Five Employer Partners exceeds the applicable Concentration Limit.
Top-Up: means a Further Advance made by a member of the Seller Group or any successor thereto, to a Borrower under a Borrower Agreement after the Origination Date of the related Receivable.
“Top-Up Receivable” means a Receivable that is, or has been, the subject of a Top-Up.
“Total Receivables Balance” means, at any time, an amount equal to the aggregate principal amount outstanding in respect of all Purchased Receivables at that time.
“Transaction Default Rate” means: (a) the Senior Interest Rate; or (b) the Mezzanine Note Interest Rate, plus 2.00 per cent., in each case.

“Transaction Documents” means: (a) the Master Framework Agreement, the Senior Facility Agreement, the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, the Subordinated Facility Agreement, the Receivables Purchase Agreement, the Servicing Agreement, the Security Agreement, each Scottish Declaration of Trust, each Scottish Assignation in Security, each Swap Agreement, each Collections Account Declaration of Trust, the Share Trust Deed, the Cash Management Agreement, the Issuer Account Bank Agreement, the Corporate Services Agreement, the Agency Fee Letter, the Senior Interest Rate and Fee Letter, the Mezzanine Interest Rate and Fee Letter, any Mezzanine Note, the Seller Power of Attorney and the Servicer Power of Attorney; (b) any ancillary agreement entered into in connection with any agreement listed in sub-paragraph (a) above and/or the Transaction more generally (including, without limitation, any document or agreement purporting to amend or amend and restate any agreement listed in sub-paragraph (a) and any agreement purporting to create supplemental Security for the benefit of the Secured Creditors from time to time); and (c) any other agreement or document agreed by the Facility Agent, the Issuer and the Seller, to be a Transaction Document.

“Transaction Party” means each of the Facility Agent, the Cash Manager, the Security Trustee, the Corporate Services Provider, the Share Trustee, the Issuer, each Senior Lender, each Mezzanine Note Purchaser, each Mezzanine Funding Agent, any Swap Provider, the Seller, the Issuer, the Registrar, the Secured Creditors, the Servicer, any Successor Servicer and the Subordinated Lender.

“Transaction Security” means the Security Agreement, each Scottish Assignation in Security and any other Security Interest granted by the Issuer pursuant to the Security Agreement and/or each Scottish Assignation in Security or any other document that may at any time be given as security or create or grant Security for any liabilities or obligations of the Issuer.

Transfer Certificate: means a certificate executed by an existing lender and a new lender to effect the transfer of all or part of the existing lender's commitment and rights under the facility agreement to the new lender.

“Transfer Date” means: (a) in relation to any assignment or transfer of a Commitment in accordance with the Senior Facility Agreement, the Senior Facility Transfer Date; or (b) in relation to any assignment or transfer of a Mezzanine Commitment in accordance with clause 13 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement, the proposed transfer date specified in the relevant letter, Assignment Agreement or Commitment Transfer Certificate, as the case may be.

“Treaty Senior Lender” means a Senior Lender that is beneficially entitled to the interest payable to it and: (a) is treated as a resident of a Treaty State for the purposes of the Treaty; (b) does not carry on a business in the United Kingdom through a permanent establishment with which a Senior Lender’s participation in the Senior Facility is effectively connected; and (c) is entitled, under the terms of the Treaty, to claim full exemption from tax imposed by the United Kingdom on interest paid in respect of the Senior Facility (subject to the completion of procedural formalities).
“Trust Property” means the beneficial interests of the Issuer in the Collections Accounts Trust declared pursuant to the Collections Account Declarations of Trust.

“UK Bail-In Legislation” means Part I of the United Kingdom Banking Act 2009 and any other law or regulation applicable in the United Kingdom relating to the resolution of unsound or failing banks, investment firms or other financial institutions or their affiliates (otherwise than through liquidation, administration or other insolvency proceedings).

“UK Binding Technical Standards” or “UK BTS” means any applicable binding technical standards made under the UK Securitisation Regulation (including, without limitation, any regulatory or implementing technical standards of the European Union retained under the domestic laws of the United Kingdom as “retained EU law” by operation of the EUWA 2018 (as amended by the EUWA 2020) (as may be amended, supplemented or replaced, from time to time)).

“UK Reporting Requirements” means the requirements of Article 7 of the UK Securitisation Regulation (together with any implementing or delegated regulations, technical standards and official guidance related thereto as may be amended, replaced or supplemented from time to time).

“UK Sec Reg Disclosure Standards” means Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1224 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1225 as retained under the domestic laws of the United Kingdom as “retained EU law” by operation of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 (as may be amended, supplemented or replaced, from time to time) and any other binding technical standards adopted in accordance with Article 7(4) of the UK Securitisation Regulation from time to time.

“UK Securitisation Regulation” means Regulation (EU) 2017/2402 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2017 as “retained EU law”, by operation of the EUWA 2018 (as amended by the EUWA 2020) and as amended by the Securitisation (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (and as may be further amended, supplemented or replaced, from time to time), together with any UK Securitisation Rules.

“UK Securitisation Rules” means: (a) any applicable UK Binding Technical Standards made under the UK Securitisation Regulation; (b) any relevant standstill decisions, guidance and policy statements relating to the application of the UK Securitisation Regulation (or any binding technical standards) published by the Prudential Regulation Authority and/or the Financial Conduct Authority (or their successors); (c) any other relevant transitional, saving or other provision relevant to the UK Securitisation Regulation by virtue of the operation of the EUWA 2018 (as amended by the EUWA 2020) (as may be amended, supplemented or replaced from time to time); and (d) any other applicable statutory instruments enacted relating to the UK Securitisation Regulation, in each case, as may be further amended, supplemented or replaced, from time to time.

“Unallocated Cash” means with respect to any Receivable, all cash collections and other cash proceeds, including, without limitation, all VAT and cash proceeds of Related Rights which, in each case, have not been identified by the Servicer as relating to a specific Purchased Receivable or any other specific Receivable.

Unassigned Receivables: means Receivables which were intended to be purchased by the Issuer but which were not validly assigned or held on trust, often due to a breach of eligibility criteria or failure to comply with perfection requirements, and are held on trust by the Seller for the Issuer.

“Unpaid Sum” means any sum due and payable under any Transaction Document or in respect of any judgment or decree of any court awarded against a Transaction Party in connection with the Transaction Documents, that was not paid on its due date.

“US Risk Retention Disclosure Memo” means the memorandum on the determination of fair value of the Subordinated Lender’s holding of the Subordinated Loan as “sponsor” (as defined under the US Risk Retention Requirements), as provided by the Subordinated Lender to the Mezzanine Funding Agent on or prior to the Signing Date.
“US Risk Retention Requirements” means the final rules contained in Regulation RR, 17 C.F.R. §246.1, et seq.
“Value” means, in respect of any person or group, the pre-money valuation as at its most recent equity investment round.

“Weekly Utilisation Date” means any Business Day of any calendar week during the Revolving Period provided that: (a) not more than one date occurs in any single calendar week; and (b) no date shall occur in any calendar week in which the Monthly Payment Date occurs, and shall not be on any Monthly Servicer Reporting Date or a date between the Monthly Servicer Reporting Date and the Monthly Payment Date (noting, for the avoidance of doubt, that a Senior Utilisation Date may still occur on a Monthly Payment Date.

“Weighted Average APR” means an annual percentage rate, equal to the weighted average annual percentage rate chargeable in respect of all Eligible Receivables (weighted by Outstanding Principal Balance).

“Write-down and Conversion Powers” means: (a) in relation to any Bail-In Legislation described in the EU Bail-In Legislation Schedule from time to time, the powers described as such in relation to that Bail-In Legislation in the EU Bail-In Legislation Schedule; (b) in relation to the UK Bail-In Legislation, any powers under that UK Bail-In Legislation to cancel, transfer or dilute shares issued by a person that is a bank or investment firm or other financial institution or affiliate of a bank, investment firm or other financial institution, to cancel, reduce, modify or change the form of a liability of such a person or any contract or instrument under which that liability arises, to convert all or part of that liability into shares, securities or obligations of that person or any other person, to provide that any such contract or instrument is to have effect as if a right had been exercised under it or to suspend any obligation in respect of that liability or any of the powers under that UK Bail-In Legislation that are related to or ancillary to any of those powers; and (c) in relation to any other applicable Bail-In Legislation: (i) any powers under that Bail-In Legislation to cancel, transfer or dilute shares issued by a person that is a bank or investment firm or other financial institution or affiliate of a bank, investment firm or other financial institution, to cancel, reduce, modify or change the form of a liability of such a person or any contract or instrument under which that liability arises, to convert all or part of that liability into shares, securities or obligations of that person or any other person, to provide that any such contract or instrument is to have effect as if a right had been exercised under it or to suspend any obligation in respect of that liability or any of the powers under that Bail-In Legislation that are related to or ancillary to any of those powers; and (ii) any similar or analogous powers under that Bail-In Legislation.

“acting in concert” means, a group of persons who, pursuant to an agreement or understanding (whether formal or informal), actively co-operate, through the acquisition, directly or indirectly, of shares in a person by any of them, either directly or indirectly, to obtain or consolidate control of that person;

“continuing” means: (a) in respect of an Early Amortisation Event, Potential Early Amortisation Event, Insolvency Event, Servicer Termination Event, Potential Servicer Termination Event, Potential Event of Default and Event of Default, that the relevant event has not been waived by the Facility Agent acting on a Most Senior Lender Instruction; (b) in respect of a Mezzanine Event of Default or Potential Mezzanine Event of Default, that the relevant event has not been waived by the Mezzanine Funding Agent acting on the instructions of the Mezzanine Note Purchasers; or (c) in any case where a cure period or remedy period is provided for in the Transaction Documents, the relevant event has not been otherwise cured or remedied in a manner expressly set out in the Transaction Documents for the cure or remedy of such event prior to the expiry of the relevant cure period or remedy period;

“control” means: (i) where a person (“P”) is treated as having control of a company (“C”) if P: (A) exercises; (B) is able to exercise; or (C) is entitled to acquire, direct or indirect control over C’s affairs; (ii) in particular, P is treated as having control of C if P possesses or is entitled to acquire: (A) more than 50% of the share capital or issued share capital of C; (B) more than 50% of the voting power in C; (C) so much of the issued share capital of C as would, on the assumption that the whole of the income of C were distributed among the participators, entitle P to receive more than 50% of the amount so distributed; or (D) such rights as would entitle P, in the event of the winding up of C or in any other circumstances, to receive more than 50% of the assets of C which would then be available for distribution among the participators; (iii) any rights that P or any other person has as a loan creditor are to be disregarded for the purposes of the assumption in paragraph (ii)(C) above; and (iv) if two or more persons together, pursuant to an agreement or understanding (whether formal or informal), actively co-operate to obtain or consolidate control, either directly or indirectly, and satisfy any of the conditions in paragraphs (i) or (ii), they are treated as having control of C.

“originate”, “origination” or “originated” means, in respect of any Receivable, the time at which the Receivable is initially recorded in the systems of the Seller as a Receivable owing by the Borrower;

Commitment Renewal Offer: means an offer made by the Issuer (following a request of the Seller) to the lenders to extend or renew the Senior Commitments or Mezzanine Commitments, specifying the proposed terms of such extension or renewal.
“Commitment Extension Notice” means a letter sent by the Senior Lenders to the Issuer (copying each of the Seller and Servicer) setting out the revised Programme Scheduled Termination Date

“Mezzanine Commitment Extension Notice” means a letter sent by the Mezzanine Note Purchasers to the Issuer (copying each of the Seller and Servicer) setting out the revised Programme Scheduled Termination Date

“Blocking Action” means performing any act (including, without limitation, refusing to sign any amendment to the Master Framework Agreement or any other Transaction Document that is not a Basic Term Modification) to block, prohibit or hinder the action from being taken by the other relevant parties unless such act would be unlawful

“Enforcement Notification” means a notification from the Facility Agent to the Mezzanine Funding Agent if the Most Senior Lenders instruct the Facility Agent to instruct the Security Trustee: (a) to deliver a Security Enforcement Notice or to take any step to enforce any Transaction Security; or (b) to instruct a Receiver to sell, lease or dispose of the Transaction Security.
“Enforcement Consultation Request” means a request by the Mezzanine Funding Agent for discussions regarding the proposed enforcement with the Most Senior Lenders
“Enforcement Consultation Period” means a maximum of five Business Days beginning on the day of the Enforcement Consultation Request

“Purchase Notice” means notice in writing to the Senior Lenders by the Mezzanine Note Purchasers to purchase all (but not part) of the outstanding Senior Loans for a purchase price equal to the Senior Lender Buyout Amount
“Eligibility Criteria Letter” means a letter entered into between the parties confirming the new Eligibility Criteria in writing
“Concentration Limit Letter” means a letter entered into between the parties confirming the new Concentration Limit in writing
“Concentration Limit Breach” means if, on any date, any of the Concentration Limits are breached

“Mezzanine Transaction” means any refinancing of the Mezzanine Notes; or transaction to provide any other mezzanine financing proposed to be entered into by [PARTY_NAME] or any of its Affiliates to be established for the benefit of it or any member of the Seller Group

“Recovering Funding Party” means any Funding Party that obtains a payment from the Issuer, any other party to a Transaction Document or otherwise (whether voluntary, involuntary or through the exercise of any right of setoff, any claim for breach of representation, warranty or undertaking or otherwise) on account of the portion of any Senior Loan or Mezzanine Note owned by it (other than pursuant to any fee payable in accordance with clause 17 (Fees) of the Senior Facility Agreement, clause 9 (Fees) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement or arising as a result of the different methods for calculating the SONIA Benchmark Rate) in excess of its rateable share of any payment on account of the Senior Loan or Mezzanine Notes held by it or in priority to the payment it would have received in accordance with the applicable Priority of Payments, pursuant to the Transaction Documents

Recovered Amount: means the amount received or recovered by a Recovering Funding Party in excess of its rateable share (after deducting purchase costs or other applicable expenses) which it is required to turn over to the Sharing Funding Parties to ensure pro rata payment distribution.
“Sharing Funding Parties” means the Funding Parties other than the Recovering Funding Party which are within the same Class of Funding Party
“Sharing Payment” means an amount equal to such receipt or recovery less any amount which the Recovering Funding Party is entitled to retain as its share of such payment received from the Issuer

“Redistributed Amount” means an amount equal to the appropriate part of its share of the Sharing Payment (together with an amount as is necessary to reimburse that Recovering Funding Party for its proportion of any interest on the Sharing Payment which that Recovering Funding Party is required to pay)

“Minimum Required Interest” means a material net economic interest in the securitisation retained by the Seller in its capacity as an “originator” on an ongoing basis by providing the Subordinated Loan, which has an aggregate principal balance of not less than five per cent. of the nominal value of the Purchased Receivables in accordance with Article 6(3)(d) of the Securitisation Regulations

“Reporting Requirements” means the requirements of Article 7 of the Securitisation Regulations (such requirements together with any implementing or delegated regulations, technical standards and official guidance related thereto as may be amended, replaced or supplemented from time to time)
“Sponsor” means the Subordinated Lender in such capacity as defined under the US Risk Retention Requirements

“Retained Interest” means an “eligible horizontal residual interest” (as defined in the US Risk Retention Requirements), in the form of the Subordinated Loan, having a fair value equal to at least 5% fair value, as of the Closing Date, of all “ABS interests” (as defined in the US Risk Retention Requirements) issued by the Issuer as part of the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Documents, using a fair value measurement framework under United States generally accepted accounting principles

“Indemnified Amounts” means any claim, loss, liability, judgment, cost, expense or any other amount (including, without limitation, interest, damages, penalties and properly incurred attorney’s fees) imposed, incurred by, asserted or awarded against the Affected Person (other than any Excluded Indemnified Amount)

“Break Costs” means an amount equal to any cost, increased cost (other than any increased cost in respect of any Regulatory Requirement which will be separately indemnified in accordance with Clause 6.4 below), broken funding cost (including, any termination cost relating to any hedging arrangement) or Reduced Rate of Return incurred or suffered by that Affected Person in connection with any Senior Facility or Mezzanine Note

Excluded Indemnified Amount: means any amount where: (a) a final judgment or decree determines that the Indemnified Amount results from the gross negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct of the party requiring indemnification; (b) the amount is recoverable under specific Tax indemnities; (c) the amount arises from credit risk (bankruptcy, insolvency or lack of creditworthiness of a Borrower); or (d) the amount comprises Excluded Taxes.

Issuer Indemnity: means the indemnity provided by the Issuer to Affected Persons in respect of all reasonable fees, out-of-pocket costs, and expenses (including legal fees and Irrecoverable VAT) properly incurred in connection with the preservation or enforcement of rights under the Transaction Documents, amendments, waivers, or other standard indemnity events.

Issuer Additional Payment: means an additional amount payable by the Issuer to a Finance Party to ensure that, after a required Tax deduction or withholding, the Finance Party receives the net amount it would have received had no such deduction been made (tax gross-up).

“Affected Person Tax Credit” means a refund of Tax or credit against Tax on its overall net income obtained by an Affected Person which receives an Issuer Additional Payment by reason of that Issuer Additional Payment

“After Tax Basis” means an amount that shall ensure that after payment of the Tax charged (and taking account of the Tax effect of any loss giving rise to the right to an indemnity) the Affected Person will have received the amount that it would have otherwise received under the indemnity or obligation but for the imposition of the charge or Tax
“Reporting FI” means the party that would be required to report such account
Connected Person: means, in respect of a relevant party, any shareholder, officer, agent, employee or director of such party.
Claims: means any amount, claim or obligation due or owing to it by the Issuer
QFC Credit Support: means support, through a guarantee or otherwise, for any agreement or instrument that is a QFC provided by the Transaction Documents
Supported QFC: means any agreement or instrument that is a QFC for which the Transaction Documents provide support

U.S. Special Resolution Regimes: means the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and Title II of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (together with the regulations promulgated thereunder)
Covered Party: means a Covered Entity that is party to a Supported QFC

Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage: means the maximum permitted percentage of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that may be comprised of receivables owed by Near Prime Borrowers subject to Adjusted Loan Terms (e.g. 4.0 per cent).

Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means, as at any date, the amount by which: (a) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that have been subject to/originated as a result of Adjusted Loan Terms advanced to Borrowers that have been classified as Near Prime Borrowers in accordance with the Seller’s underwriting policies and where the amended monthly payment is greater than the original monthly payment; exceeds (b) the amount calculated by multiplying the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables at that date by the Adjusted Loan Terms Near Prime Borrowers Concentration Percentage

Direct Debit/Push Payments Concentration Percentage: means the maximum permitted percentage of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that may be comprised of receivables where the Borrower pays by way of direct debit or Push Payments (e.g. 19.0 per cent).

Direct Debit/Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount: means, as at any date, the amount by which: (a) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Borrowers that are paying through direct debit or Push Payment for at least two consecutive calendar months (instead of by way of Salary Deduction); exceeds (b) the amount calculated by multiplying the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables at that date by the Direct Debit/Push Payments Concentration Percentage

Maximum Average Weighted Remaining Term Excess Concentration Amount: means, as at any date, the amount that is equal to the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are required to be excluded from the calculation of the aggregate weighted average remaining term of the Purchased Receivables so that the aggregate weighted average remaining term of the Purchased Receivables does not exceed the Maximum Average Weighted Remaining Term (and, for the purposes of selecting the relevant Purchased Receivables for exclusion, the Purchased Receivables shall be selected so that the Purchased Receivable that reduces the aggregate weighted average remaining term of the Purchased Receivables by the greatest amount is excluded first).

Weighted Average APR Excess Concentration Amount: means, as at any date, the amount that is equal to the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are required to be excluded from the calculation of the Minimum Weighted Average APR so that it exceeds the sum of the aggregate weighted average Swap Rate in respect of the Purchased Receivables and the applicable margin specified in the Transaction Documents (and, for the purposes of selecting the relevant Purchased Receivables for exclusion, the Purchased Receivables shall be selected so that the Purchased Receivable that reduces the aggregate weighted average Swap Rate of the Purchased Receivables by the greatest amount is excluded first).
Statement: means a representation, warranty or statement made, or deemed to be made, by the Seller under or in connection with any Transaction Document

breach: means, in relation to a Statement, that it proves to be incorrect, inaccurate or untrue in any material respect (or if any Statement is already qualified by materiality, it proves to be incorrect, inaccurate or untrue) when made, or deemed to be made

Authorisation: means all authorisations, consents, licences, filings, approvals and permissions, including, where relevant, as required by the Financial Conduct Authority or under Data Protection Laws required to enable it to duly execute, deliver, exercise its rights under and perform its obligations under the Transaction Documents to which it is or shall be a party or any other document to be delivered by it under any Transaction Document

Blocking Law: means (i) Council Regulation (EC) 2271/96 (or any law or regulation implementing such Regulation in any member state of the European Union), (ii) any similar law or regulation in the United Kingdom, or (iii) Section 7 of the German Foreign Trade Regulation (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung)

Privacy Commitments: means (i) the Data Protection Laws, (ii) contractual obligations and other commitments, and (iii) its own policies and procedures, in each case as relating to privacy, data protection, and the processing of Personal Data

Relevant Notice: means a notice issued by the Security Trustee (or equivalent) confirming that its rights as chargee, assignee or beneficiary under the relevant Security Documents have become exercisable.
Erroneous Payment: means a payment of an amount by the Facility Agent to another Transaction Party which the Facility Agent determines (in its sole discretion) was made in error
Information: means any analysis, model, compilation, study, report or other document produced in connection with the Transaction Documents
